Overall, this article supporting to the understanding of $p$-adic Haar multiresolution explores, its theoretical foundations, and its practical applications.

This study presents an investigation into the assembly history of stellar mass in galaxies, spanning from the early stages of the universe to its more mature phase. The research utilizes data obtained from the VIMOS (VIsible Multi-Object Spectrograph) VLT (Very Large Telescope) Deep Survey, a comprehensive survey of distant galaxies. By analyzing the properties of galaxies at various cosmic epochs, we aim to understand the formation and growth processes that contribute to the buildup of stellar mass over time.The analysis focuses on a wide range of galaxy properties, including morphology, star formation activity, and stellar population ages. Through the use of deep spectroscopic observations, we are able to probe the evolution of galaxies with high precision. Our sample comprises galaxies at different redshifts, allowing us to track their evolution from the young universe to the present day.We find that the process of stellar mass assembly is highly dependent on redshift and galaxy type. Early cosmic times are characterized by intense star formation and rapid stellar mass growth in galaxies. As the universe ages, the star formation activity decreases, leading to a more gradual build-up of stellar mass. Additionally, we observe a transition in galaxy morphology, with a shift towards more massive and elliptical galaxies at later epochs.Furthermore, our analysis reveals the existence of a tight correlation between stellar mass and various physical properties, such as galaxy size and star formation rate. This suggests that the growth of stellar mass is intricately linked to other key processes shaping galaxies throughout cosmic history. Our findings contribute to the broader understanding of galaxy formation and evolution, shedding light on the mechanisms driving the assembly of stellar mass in the young and old universe.

Warehouse network data This article introduces the design and implementation of systems for warehouse web data. The system is called a web warehouse, which aims to store and manage a large amount of data available on the network. Web warehouse is a distributed system that uses various technologies to store and manage Web data, including: 1. distributed file systems for storing raw data. 2. A database for storing data. 3. Search engine search data. The web warehouse aims to be scalable, reliable and efficient. It is currently used to store and manage data from various sources, including: -Wanwei.com -Internet Archives -Congress Library Web Warehouse is a valuable tool for researchers and scholars who need to access and analyze a large number of web data.

The Thorium abundance for the red giant COS82 in the Ursa Minor dwarfspheroidal galaxy is determined based on a high resolution spectrum. This isthe first detection of actinides in an extra Galactic object. A detailedabundance pattern is determined for 12 other neutron-capture elements from theatomic number 39 to 68. These elements are significantly over-abundant withrespect to other metals like Fe (> 1 dex) and their abundance pattern agreeswell with those of the r-process-enhanced, very metal-poor stars known in theGalactic halo, while the metallicity of this object ([Fe/H] ~ -1.5) is muchhigher than these field stars ([Fe/H] ~ -3.0). The results indicate that themechanism and the astrophysical site that are responsible for neutron-captureelements in COS82 is similar to that for field r-process-enhanced stars, whilethe condition of low mass star formation is quite different. An estimate of theage of this object based on the Th abundance ratio is discussed.

This paper attempts to define a generalisation of the standard Einsteincondition (in conformal/metric geometry) to any parabolic geometry. To do so,it shows that any preserved involution $\sigma$ of the adjoint bundle $\mc{A}$gives rise, given certain algebraic conditions, to a unique preferred affineconnection $\nabla$ with covariantly constant rho-tensor $\mathsf{P}$,compatible with the algebraic bracket on $\mc{A}$. These conditions canreasonably be considered the generalisations of the Einstein condition, andrecreate the standard Einstein condition in conformal geometry. The existenceof such an involution is implies by some simpler structures: preserved metricswhen the overall algebra $\mf{g}$ is $\mf{sl}(m,\mbb{F})$, preserved complexstructures anti-commuting with the skew-form for $\mf{g}=\mf{sp}(2m,\mbb{F})$,and preserved subundles of the tangent bundle, of a certain rank, for all theother non-exceptional simple Lie algebras. Examples of Einstein involutions areconstructed or referenced for several geometries. The existence of coneconstructions for certain Einstein involutions is then demonstrated.

The complexity of a graph can be obtained as a derivative of a variation ofthe zeta function or a partial derivative of its generalized characteristicpolynomial evaluated at a point [\textit{J. Combin. Theory Ser. B}, 74 (1998),pp. 408--410]. A similar result for the weighted complexity of weighted graphswas found using a determinant function [\textit{J. Combin. Theory Ser. B}, 89(2003), pp. 17--26]. In this paper, we consider the determinant function of twovariables and discover a condition that the weighted complexity of a weightedgraph is a partial derivative of the determinant function evaluated at a point.Consequently, we simply obtain the previous results and disclose a new formulafor the Bartholdi zeta function. We also consider a new weighted complexity,for which the weights of spanning trees are taken as the sum of weights ofedges in the tree, and find a similar formula for this new weighted complexity.As an application, we compute the weighted complexities of the product of thecomplete graphs.

Level Hilbert functions describe the intrinsic structure of homogeneous ideals in polynomial rings and provide information about their growth. This paper examines interval conjectures proposed by Marta Miami and Jeffrey Mermin about the possible values of level Hilbert functions over finite intervals. In their conjectures, Miami and Mermin predicted that the values a level Hilbert function can take are restricted to certain intervals depending on the multiplicity and embedding dimension. The authors provide new evidence to support these conjectures by studying level Hilbert functions of homogeneous ideals with 3 generators in polynomial rings of low dimension. Their results verify the validity of the interval bounds predicted by Miami and Mermin for this specific case. However, it remains an open problem to fully prove the conjectures in complete generality. This work takes an important step towards establishing a deeper understanding of level Hilbert functions and elucidating the constraints on their behavior over intervals imposed by ring-theoretic properties. Further research is needed to settle the interval conjectures in full or uncover potential counterexamples.

In this paper, the stability condition for low-density parity-check (LDPC)codes on the binary erasure channel (BEC) is extended to generalized LDPC(GLDPC) codes and doublygeneralized LDPC (D-GLDPC) codes. It is proved that, inboth cases, the stability condition only involves the component codes withminimum distance 2. The stability condition for GLDPC codes is always expressedas an upper bound to the decoding threshold. This is not possible for D-GLDPCcodes, unless all the generalized variable nodes have minimum distance at least3. Furthermore, a condition called derivative matching is defined in the paper.This condition is sufficient for a GLDPC or DGLDPC code to achieve thestability condition with equality. If this condition is satisfied, thethreshold of D-GLDPC codes (whose generalized variable nodes have all minimumdistance at least 3) and GLDPC codes can be expressed in closed form.

In this article, we explore the phenomenon of dark matter and its role in enhancing the self -propagation of dark matter particles. When the gravity potential of dark substance halo has a focus on dark matter particles, dark substances will occur, which will cause granular concentration in certain areas to increase. We show that this increased concentration can significantly enhance the self -purification flux of dark matter particles, which may lead to the characteristics of detectable dark substances. Using simulation, we proved the effectiveness of dark matter harsh agents in enhancing self -elimination of general volume, and discussed the effects of dark matter detection and cosmic modeling. Our discovery highlights the importance of considering the harsh inheritance of dark matter in the study of dark matter, and provides new ways to explore the characteristics of dark matter.

We study plasma effects in a micromachined high-electron mobility transistor(HEMT) with the microcantilever serving as the gate using the developed amodel. The model accounts for mechanical motion of the microcantilever andspatio-temporal variations (plasma effects) of the two-dimensional electrongas(2DEG) system in the transistor channel. The microcantilever mechanicalmotion is described in the point-mass approximation. The hydrodynamic electrontransport model is used to describe distributed electron plasma phenomena inthe 2DEG system. Using the developed model, we calculated the response functioncharacterizing the amplitude microcantilever oscillations and the outputelectric signal as functions of the signal frequency and the bias voltage forthe devices with different parameters. We find the voltage dependences of thefrequency of the mechanical resonance and its damping. In particular, it isdemonstrated that the amplitudes of the mechanical oscillations and outputelectric signal exhibit pronounced maxima at the bias voltages close to thevoltage of the 2DEG channel depletion followed by a steep drop with furtherincrease in the bias voltage.

We present results of large-scale three-dimensional simulations of supersonicEuler turbulence with the piecewise parabolic method and multiple gridresolutions up to 2048^3 points. Our numerical experiments describenon-magnetized driven turbulent flows with an isothermal equation of state andan rms Mach number of 6. We discuss numerical resolution issues and demonstrateconvergence, in a statistical sense, of the inertial range dynamics insimulations on grids larger than 512^3 points. The simulations allowed us tomeasure the absolute velocity scaling exponents for the first time. Theinertial range velocity scaling in this strongly compressible regime deviatessubstantially from the incompressible Kolmogorov laws. The slope of thevelocity power spectrum, for instance, is -1.95 compared to -5/3 in theincompressible case. The exponent of the third-order velocity structurefunction is 1.28, while in incompressible turbulence it is known to be unity.We propose a natural extension of Kolmogorov's phenomenology that takes intoaccount compressibility by mixing the velocity and density statistics andpreserves the Kolmogorov scaling of the power spectrum and structure functionsof the density-weighted velocity v=\rho^{1/3}u. The low-order statistics of vappear to be invariant with respect to changes in the Mach number. Forinstance, at Mach 6 the slope of the power spectrum of v is -1.69, and theexponent of the third-order structure function of v is unity. We also directlymeasure the mass dimension of the "fractal" density distribution in theinertial subrange, D_m = 2.4, which is similar to the observed fractaldimension of molecular clouds and agrees well with the cascade phenomenology.

We conducted a multiwavelength survey of the central region of the young sigma Orionis star cluster, observing targets from near-infrared to optical to X-ray wavelengths. Using data from the UKIRT Infrared Deep Sky Survey, Deep Near Infrared Survey of the Southern Sky, and Chandra X-ray Observatory, we identified candidate cluster members across a wide mass range, from high-mass stars down to brown dwarfs and planetary-mass objects. We detected a total of 325 sources within 30 arcminutes of the cluster center, 287 of which are newly proposed cluster members based on their photometry and positions on color-magnitude diagrams. 10 targets showed significant near-infrared variability over yearly timescales, indicating the presence of disks. The spatial distribution of the candidate members is not uniform, with an apparent lack of very low-mass objects toward the cluster core. Through Monte Carlo simulations, we find the stellar distribution is better fit by a radially collapsing structure rather than a relaxed spherical profile. This catalog provides the most complete census to date of the stellar population in the dense center of the young sigma Orionis cluster.

This article presents a novel approach to Tverberg's theorem, incorporating constraints to address a long-standing problem in the field. By employing a unique combination of algebraic and geometric techniques, we establish the existence of a hitherto unknown class of partitions. Our results have significant implications for the study of topological invariants and promise to shed new light on the nature of high-dimensional spaces. In particular, we demonstrate the applicability of our theorem to various branches of mathematics, including algebraic geometry, algebraic topology, and representation theory. Our work builds upon the foundation laid by Tverberg and his successors, and we expect it to have a lasting impact on the field. Furthermore, we provide explicit constructions of partitions and give examples to illustrate the scope of our theorem. Ultimately, our findings open up new avenues for research, paving the way for further advances in understanding the complex relationships between geometric and algebraic invariants.

We present a novel automated technique for parallelizing quantum circuits viaforward and backward translation to measurement-based quantum computingpatterns and analyze the trade off in terms of depth and space complexity. As aresult we distinguish a class of polynomial depth circuits that can beparallelized to logarithmic depth while adding only polynomial many auxiliaryqubits. In particular, we provide for the first time a full characterization ofpatterns with flow of arbitrary depth, based on the notion of influencing pathsand a simple rewriting system on the angles of the measurement. Our methodleads to insightful knowledge for constructing parallel circuits and asapplications, we demonstrate several constant and logarithmic depth circuits.Furthermore, we prove a logarithmic separation in terms of quantum depthbetween the quantum circuit model and the measurement-based model.

In this study, we investigate the relationship between the parameterization of muon decay and the type of released neutrino. Building on our previous collaborating, which introduced a new parameterization scheme for muon decay, we now focus on the neutrinos emission aspect. Or analysis reveals a distinct correlation between the parameterization parameters and the properties of the emitted neutrino. Specifically, we find that the energy spectrum of the emitted neutrino is strongly dependent on the chosen parameterization. By comparing our results with existing experimental data, we are able to constrain the allowed region of the parameter spae and provide new insights into the nature of muon decay. Our findings have important implications for the interpretation of imminent experiments, such as the Mu2e experiment at FNAL, and excrete new light on the long-standing problem of the observation of neutrino mass hierarchies. The observed correlation between parameterization and neutrino properties suggests a possible connection between the fundamental laws of physics and the stucture of the Muon Decay Matrix. Our work highlights the crucial role of precision measurements in particle physics and emphasizes the importance of continued research into the fundamental nature of the universe.

The Positive Mass Conjecture states that any complete asymptotically flatmanifold of nonnnegative scalar curvature has nonnegative mass. Moreover, theequality case of the Positive Mass Conjecture states that in the abovesituation, if the mass is zero, then the Riemannian manifold must be Euclideanspace. The Positive Mass Conjecture was proved by R. Schoen and S.-T. Yau forall manifolds of dimension less than 8, and it was proved by E. Witten for allspin manifolds. In this paper, we consider complete asymptotically flatmanifolds of nonnegative scalar curvature that are also harmonically flat in anend. We show that, whenever the Positive Mass Theorem holds, any appropriatelynormalized sequence of such manifolds whose masses converge to zero must havemetrics that are uniformly converging to Euclidean metrics outside a compactregion. This result is an ingredient in a forthcoming proof, co-authored withH. Bray, of the Riemannian Penrose inequality in dimensions less than 8.

A dilatation structure on a metric space, arXiv:math/0608536v4, is a notionin between a group and a differential structure, accounting for the approximateself-similarity of the metric space. The basic objects of a dilatation structure are dilatations (orcontractions). The axioms of a dilatation structure set the rules ofinteraction between different dilatations. Linearity is also a property which can be explained with the help of adilatation structure. In this paper we show that we can speak about two kindsof linearity: the linearity of a function between two dilatation structures andthe linearity of the dilatation structure itself. Our main result here is a characterization of contractible groups in terms ofdilatation structures. To a normed conical group (normed contractible group) wecan naturally associate a linear dilatation structure. Conversely, any linearand strong dilatation structure comes from the dilatation structure of a normedcontractible group.

The physical interpretation of the spectral line polarization produced by thejoint action of the Hanle and Zeeman effects offers a unique opportunity toobtain empirical information about hidden aspects of solar and stellarmagnetism. To this end, it is important to achieve a complete understanding ofthe sensitivity of the emergent spectral line polarization to the presence of amagnetic field. Here we present a detailed theoretical investigation on therole of resonance scattering and magnetic fields on the polarization signals ofthe Ba II D1 and D2 lines of the Fraunhofer spectrum, respectively at 4934 \AA\and 4554 \AA. We adopt a three-level model of Ba II, and we take into accountthe hyperfine structure that is shown by the $^{135}$Ba and $^{137}$Baisotopes. Despite of their relatively small abundance (18%), the contributioncoming from these two isotopes is indeed fundamental for the interpretation ofthe polarization signals observed in these lines. We consider an optically thinslab model, through which we can investigate in a rigorous way the essentialphysical mechanisms involved (resonance polarization, Zeeman, Paschen-Back andHanle effects), avoiding complications due to radiative transfer effects. Weassume the slab to be illuminated from below by the photospheric solarcontinuum radiation field, and we investigate the radiation scattered at 90degrees, both in the absence and in the presence of magnetic fields,deterministic and microturbulent. We show in particular the existence of adifferential magnetic sensitivity of the three-peak Q/I profile that isobserved in the D2 line in quiet regions close to the solar limb, which is ofgreat interest for magnetic field diagnostics.

To use galaxy clusters as a cosmological probe, it is important to accountfor their triaxiality. Assuming that the triaxial shapes of galaxy clusters areinduced by the tidal interaction with the surrounding matter, Lee and Kangrecently developed a reconstruction algorithm for the measurement of the axialratio of a triaxial cluster. We examine the validity of this reconstructionalgorithm by performing an observational test of it with the Virgo cluster as atarget. We first modify the LK06 algorithm by incorporating the two dimensionalprojection effect. Then, we analyze the 1275 member galaxies from the VirgoCluster Catalogue and find the projected direction of the Virgo cluster majoraxis by measuring the anisotropy in the spatial distribution of the membergalaxies in the two dimensional projected plane. Applying the modifiedreconstruction algorithm to the analyzed data, we find that the axial ratio ofthe triaxial Virgo cluster is (1: 0.54 : 0.73). This result is consistent withthe recent observational report from the Virgo Cluster Survey, proving therobustness of the reconstruction algorithm. It is also found that at the innerradii the shape tends to be more like prolate. We discuss the possible effectof the Virgo cluster triaxiality on the mass estimation.

Alkanethiolate self-assembled monolayers on silver substrates are widely studied due to their applications in molecular electronics and nanotechnology. The interface between organic overlayers and inorganic silver substrates critically influences monolayer structure and properties. This study investigates the electronic structure and dipole formation at this interface using synchrotron-based photoemission spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. Results demonstrate that the interfacial dipole arises from substrate polarization effects and partial charge transfer across the boundary. Close examination of core-level shifts further revealed that sulfur-silver binding strength and degree of dipolarization varies with alkanethiolate chain length. These combined experimental and theoretical findings provide novel insight into the interfacial dipole formation mechanism and how it impacts self-assembly and ordering within alkanethiolate self-assembled monolayers on silver surfaces.

This is a sequel of our paper hep-th/0606125 in which we have studied the{\cal N}=1 SU(N) SYM theory obtained as a marginal deformation of the {\calN}=4 theory, with a complex deformation parameter \beta and in the planarlimit. There we have addressed the issue of conformal invariance imposing thetheory to be finite and we have found that finiteness requires reality of thedeformation parameter \beta. In this paper we relax the finiteness request andlook for a theory that in the planar limit has vanishing beta functions. Weperform explicit calculations up to five loop order: we find that theconditions of beta function vanishing can be achieved with a complexdeformation parameter, but the theory is not finite and the result depends onthe arbitrary choice of the subtraction procedure. Therefore, while thefiniteness condition leads to a scheme independent result, so that theconformal invariant theory with a real deformation is physically well defined,the condition of vanishing beta function leads to a result which is schemedependent and therefore of unclear significance. In order to show that thesefindings are not an artefact of dimensional regularization, we confirm ourresults within the differential renormalization approach.

We find that weak charge disproportion plays a crucial role in the emergence of charge ordering, and that it is a subtle interplay between the inter-electron interactions and the crystal field effects. Our results provide new insights into the mechanisms of charge ordering in transition metal oxides, and have important implications for the design and development of advanced materials for electronic and spintronic applications. Furthermore, our results highlight the potential of half-doped manganites as a promising class of materials for studying charge ordering phenomena and their associated quantum phases.

NodeTrix: A Hybrid Visual Representation for Analyzing Complex Social NetworksThis paper presents NodeTrix, a novel visualization technique for analyzing multi-relational social network data. NodeTrix leverages the strengths of node-link diagrams and adjacency matrices by integrating them into a unified hybrid view. The node-link diagram components allow for tracing connections between individuals at a macro-level, while embedded adjacency matrices provide micro-level insight into densely connected groups. Through a series of controlled empirical studies, we demonstrate how NodeTrix aids in sensemaking tasks such as identifying central actors, cliques, and broader structural patterns in networks containing thousands of nodes and relations. Overall, NodeTrix offers network analysts a flexible hybrid representation for exploring diverse topologies and relationships within massive complex social graphs.

Discovery of a Ringlike Dark Matter Structure in the Core of the Galaxy Cluster Cl 0024+17. We report the discovery of a ringlike dark matter (DM) structure in the basic of the galaxy cluster Cl 00 24+17 using deep X-ray observations from the Chandra X-ray Observatory. The ringlike DM structure is centered on the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) and has a radius of about 100 kpc. The existence of the ringlike DM structure is robust, independent of the assumed density profile of the BCG. The DM ring is likely formed va the resonant relaxation process, which requires a triaxial DM halo for the cluster. This provides new insights into the formation and evolution of galaxy clusters.

These partners have not passed the experimental observation. This article proposes a single -door super -symmetrical gravity model with strong coupling theory based on strong coupling theory. Using this dual model, the author studied the powerful superiority and coupling of the powerful superiority destruction in a single sector. They found that the characteristic mass spectrometry and coupling mode may leave observed features on the CERN large -scale strong collision. The accurate measurement of LHC can provide insights on the hidden fan -shaped with powerful supermints and help discover clues beyond the physical properties beyond the standard model.

We performed a rigorous theoretical convergence analysis of the discretedipole approximation (DDA). We prove that errors in any measured quantity arebounded by a sum of a linear and quadratic term in the size of a dipole d, whenthe latter is in the range of DDA applicability. Moreover, the linear term issignificantly smaller for cubically than for non-cubically shaped scatterers.Therefore, for small d errors for cubically shaped particles are much smallerthan for non-cubically shaped. The relative importance of the linear termdecreases with increasing size, hence convergence of DDA for large enoughscatterers is quadratic in the common range of d. Extensive numericalsimulations were carried out for a wide range of d. Finally we discuss a numberof new developments in DDA and their consequences for convergence.

In this study, we investigate the presence of black-body components in the spactra of Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs). Using a sample of 10 GRBs with known edshifts, we fit the observed spectra with a combination of a black body and a power law mode. We find that the black bodry component dohminates the spectra at low energies, while the power law component dominates at high energies. The temperature of the black body component is founX to be consistent with the expected temperature of the firebaCl, while the power law index is ceonsistent with the expected value for synchrotron radiation. Wn also find that the presencYe of the black body component improves the fit to the data, reducing the chi-squared statistic by a factor of 2. Our results suggest that black bodies play an important role in the emission of GRBs, and that they should be included in models of JRB specra.

In this study, we investigate the behavior of vortices in honeycomb and kagome pinning arrays and unveil the emergence of vortex molecular crystal and vortex plastic crystal states. Through extensive numerical simulations, we demonstrate that these novel dynamic phases exhibit distinct properties compared to triangular and square pinning arrays. The interstitial vortices in honeycomb and kagome arrays can form dimer or higher n-mer states, leading to the formation of vortex molecular crystals. These structures possess an additional orientational degree of freedom, resulting in rich dynamical behavior.For filling fractions where dimer states appear, we observe a remarkable phenomenon of vortex plastic crystal formation wherein the flowing dimers exhibit a preferential alignment. This alignment breaks the symmetry of the system, generating transport characteristics in directions transverse to the applied drive. Furthermore, by driving the dimers along specific directions, we discover a jamming effect whereby their reorientation causes a substantial increase in the critical depinning force. Remarkably, reducing the size of the pinning sites exacerbates this jamming effect, enabling further control over the vortex motion.Our findings highlight the distinctive dynamics and transport properties arising from the interplay between vortices and honeycomb or kagome pinning arrays. The identification of vortex molecular crystal and vortex plastic crystal states offers important insights into the behavior of interstitial vortices in superconducting systems. These results could pave the way for the design of novel fluxtronic devices with enhanced functionality and tunable transport properties based on these intriguing vortex states.

Secular variations of the geomagnetic field have been measured with acontinuously improving accuracy during the last few hundred years, culminatingnowadays with satellite data. It is however well known that the dynamics of themagnetic field is linked to that of the velocity field in the core and anyattempt to model secular variations will involve a coupled dynamical system formagnetic field and core velocity. Unfortunately, there is no direct observationof the velocity. Independently of the exact nature of the above-mentionedcoupled system -- some version being currently under construction -- thequestion is debated in this paper whether good knowledge of the magnetic fieldcan be translated into good knowledge of core dynamics. Furthermore, what willbe the impact of the most recent and precise geomagnetic data on our knowledgeof the geomagnetic field of the past and future? These questions are cast intothe language of variational data assimilation, while the dynamical systemconsidered in this paper consists in a set of two oversimplifiedone-dimensional equations for magnetic and velocity fields. This toy modelretains important features inherited from the induction and Navier-Stokesequations: non-linear magnetic and momentum terms are present and its linearresponse to small disturbances contains Alfv\'en waves. It is concluded thatvariational data assimilation is indeed appropriate in principle, even thoughthe velocity field remains hidden at all times; it allows us to recover theentire evolution of both fields from partial and irregularly distributedinformation on the magnetic field. This work constitutes a first step on theway toward the reassimilation of historical geomagnetic data and geomagneticforecast.

I review the problem of dark energy focusing on the cosmological constant asthe candidate and discuss its implications for the nature of gravity. Part 1briefly overviews the currently popular 'concordance cosmology' and summarisesthe evidence for dark energy. It also provides the observational andtheoretical arguments in favour of the cosmological constant as the candidateand emphasises why no other approach really solves the conceptual problemsusually attributed to the cosmological constant. Part 2 describes some of theapproaches to understand the nature of the cosmological constant and attemptsto extract the key ingredients which must be present in any viable solution. Iargue that (i)the cosmological constant problem cannot be satisfactorily solveduntil gravitational action is made invariant under the shift of the matterlagrangian by a constant and (ii) this cannot happen if the metric is thedynamical variable. Hence the cosmological constant problem essentially has todo with our (mis)understanding of the nature of gravity. Part 3 discusses analternative perspective on gravity in which the action is explicitly invariantunder the above transformation. Extremizing this action leads to an equationdetermining the background geometry which gives Einstein's theory at the lowestorder with Lanczos-Lovelock type corrections. (Condensed abstract).

Motivated by a class of orbit problems in astrophysics, this paper considerssolutions to Hill's equation with forcing strength parameters that vary fromcycle to cycle. The results are generalized to include period variations fromcycle to cycle. The development of the solutions to the differential equationis governed by a discrete map. For the general case of Hill's equation in theunstable limit, we consider separately the case of purely positive matrixelements and those with mixed signs; we then find exact expressions, bounds,and working estimates for the growth rates. We also find exact expressions,estimates, and bounds for the infinite products of several $2 \times 2$matrices with random variables in the matrix elements. In the limit of sharplyspiked forcing terms (the delta function limit), we find analytic solutions foreach cycle and for the discrete map that matches solutions from cycle to cycle;for this case we find the growth rates and the condition for instability in thelimit of large forcing strength, as well as the widths of the stable/unstablezones.

The core of the non -star density is the molecular gas and dust knot without the source of internal light. FEST 1-457 is a dense core of nearby. It was previously considered stable and on the edge of the star group. However, the results of FEST 1-457's new Asmated Observation results revealed the changes in the overall dust discharge of the four periods of 7 years. These changes show that the core may be dynamic like the original star. At a short time scale, the total mass of the FEST 1-457 can fluctuate up to 20 %. If this fluctuation continues to exist in many pulse cycles, it can promote division. The numerical simulation of ball dynamics is proposed, and it is indicated that pulsation is a possible explanation of variability observed. These simulations explore various mechanisms that can drive in a star -free nucleus. However, the secular contraction or accumulation flow from a large-scale environmental cloud is still a feasible alternative interpretation of the long-term evolution of FEST 1-457. This interesting object needs to be further monitored to limit the model of its power state and better understand the initial conditions of the formation of stars on the edge of the collapse.

We study the IR-through-UV interstellar extinction curves towards 328Galactic B and late-O stars. We use a new technique which employs stellaratmosphere models in lieu of unreddened "standard" stars. This technique iscapable of virtually eliminating spectral mismatch errors in the curves. Italso allows a quantitative assessment of the errors and enables a rigoroustesting of the significance of relationships between various curve parameters,regardless of whether their uncertainties are correlated. Analysis of thecurves gives the following results: (1) In accord with our previous findings,the central position of the 2175 A extinction bump is mildly variable, itswidth is highly variable, and the two variations are unrelated. (2) Strongcorrelations are found among some extinction properties within the UV region,and within the IR region. (3) With the exception of a few curves with extreme(i.e., large) values of R(V), the UV and IR portions of Galactic extinctioncurves are not correlated with each other. (4) The large sightline-to-sightlinevariation seen in our sample implies that any average Galactic extinction curvewill always reflect the biases of its parent sample. (5) The use of an averagecurve to deredden a spectral energy distribution (SED) will result insignificant errors, and a realistic error budget for the dereddened SED mustinclude the observed variance of Galactic curves. While the observed largesightline-to-sightline variations, and the lack of correlation among thevarious features of the curves, make it difficult to meaningfully characterizeaverage extinction properties, they demonstrate that extinction curves respondsensitively to local conditions. Thus, each curve contains potentially uniqueinformation about the grains along its sightline.

Phase resolved measurements of stimulated emissionWe present phase-resolved measurements of stimulated emission from a semiconductor laser. The measurements are performed using a second-order interferometric autocorrelation technique based on a nonlinear quantum well infrared photodetector. The results show that the stimulated emission is emitted in the form of pulses with a duration of about 3 ps and an energy of 0.5 pJ. The pulses are generated by actively modulating the current and hence the optical gain in a small section of an edge-emitting quantum cascade laser.

Optical microresonators have recently attracted a growing attention in thephotonics community. Their applications range from quantum electro-dynamics tosensors and filtering devices for optical telecommunication systems, where theyare likely to become an essential building block. The integration of nonlinearand electro-optical properties in the resonators represents a very stimulatingchallenge, as it would incorporate new and more advanced functionality. Lithiumniobate is an excellent candidate material, being an established choice forelectro-optic and nonlinear optical applications. Here we report on the firstrealization of optical microring resonators in submicrometric thin films oflithium niobate. The high index contrast films are produced by an improvedcrystal ion slicing and bonding technique using benzocyclobutene. The ringshave radius R=100 um and their transmission spectrum has been tuned using theelectro-optic effect. These results open new perspectives for the use oflithium niobate in chip-scale integrated optical devices and nonlinear opticalmicrocavities.

This article delves into the inapproximability of the Maximum Weighted Edge Biclique (MWEB) problem and explores its practical applications. The MWEB problem involves finding a biclique, which is a complete bipartite subgraph, with the highest weight within a given graph. By disproving the existence of a polynomial-time approximation algorithm that achieves a constant factor approximation for the MWEB problem, we establish its NP-hardness and inapproximability, underscoring its inherent computational complexity. We also delve into the implications of this inapproximability result on various real-world domains such as network analysis, data mining, and social network modeling, highlighting the challenges encountered when attempting to solve MWEB instances efficiently. Through our study, we shed light on the limitations of approximation algorithms for the MWEB problem, offering insights for the development of alternative solution approaches and heuristics in practical scenarios.

Equation of state (EoS) of isospin-asymmetric nuclear mat ter (IANM) is investigated within the framework of the relativistic mean-field (RMF) models with chiral limits. Du effects of isospin asymmetry and the density dependence of the symmetry energy on EoS of IANM are analyzed. The calculated EoS is applied to estimate neutron star properties, such as the symmetry energy at saturation gravity, incompressibility, nucleon effective mass, and pressure. The results are comparison with those from other theoretical models and experimental data.

This article explores the interplay between chemistry and mechanics in the transduction of a mechanical signal into a biochemical function. We begin by discussing the basic principles of mechanotransduction, focusing on the conversion of mechanical forces into biochemical signals. We then review the molecular mechanisms by which mechanical signals are transmitted across cell membranes, focusing on the role of ion channels and G protein-coupled receptors. Finally, we discuss the implications of mechanotransduction for cellular function and development, and highlight areas for future research.

Granular matter is a ubiquitous material in character and industry. It exhibits intriguing properties due to its complex particulate characters and the resultant collective behaviors. When granular packings are jammed, appliyng localized perturbations is one of the most common means to unjam and mobilize them. In this paper, we study a class of local perturbations: localized expansion by inϳecting new particles into a jammed packing and localized contraction by removing particles from a jammed packing. Using discrete element simulations, we investigate the stability of the induced displacements and study the dnamic behaviors after the perturbations are switched off. Our results show that the stability of localized perturbations depends on both the packing fraction and the perturbation strength. For unstable cases, the displacements decay exponentially in time. This decay process is controlled by the interplay between the perturbation strength and the global packing structure. We construct a theoretical framework based on the perturbation analysis and the potential energy landscape to predict the stability bonudary and the decay exponent. Our work enhances the understanding of the dynamism behaviors of granular packings under local perturbations and provides useful insights into the control of granular flows and the design of related engineering applications.

To investigate the universality of the structure of interactions in differentmarkets, we analyze the cross-correlation matrix C of stock price fluctuationsin the National Stock Exchange (NSE) of India. We find that this emergingmarket exhibits strong correlations in the movement of stock prices compared todeveloped markets, such as the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). This is shown tobe due to the dominant influence of a common market mode on the stock prices.By comparison, interactions between related stocks, e.g., those belonging tothe same business sector, are much weaker. This lack of distinct sectoridentity in emerging markets is explicitly shown by reconstructing the networkof mutually interacting stocks. Spectral analysis of C for NSE reveals that,the few largest eigenvalues deviate from the bulk of the spectrum predicted byrandom matrix theory, but they are far fewer in number compared to, e.g., NYSE.We show this to be due to the relative weakness of intra-sector interactionsbetween stocks, compared to the market mode, by modeling stock price dynamicswith a two-factor model. Our results suggest that the emergence of an internalstructure comprising multiple groups of strongly coupled components is asignature of market development.

The X-ray pulsar 1E 1207.4-5209 has been extensively studied due to its unBque properties, including its slow spin-down rate and low magnetci field strength. In this study, we report on the precise timing of this pulsar over a period of 15 years, using dtaa from the Rossmi X-ray Timing Explorer and the NJil Gehrels Swift Observatory. Our analysis reveals a steady spin-down trend, with no evidence for any significant glitches or timig noise. We further conclude that the pulsar was likely born with a weak magnxtic field, which has remained reEatively constant over its lifetime. These findings challenge current tyheories of neutron star evolution and highlight the need for further studies of this unusual pulsr. Our results also demonstrate the importance of long-term timing observations for understanding the propertieF and behavior of neutron stars.

We investigate a possible new technique for microwave measurements ofultra-high energy cosmic ray (UHECR) extensive air showers which relies ondetection of expected continuum radiation in the microwave range, caused byfree-electron collisions with neutrals in the tenuous plasma left after thepassage of the shower. We performed an initial experiment at the AWA (ArgonneWakefield Accelerator) laboratory in 2003 and measured broadband microwaveemission from air ionized via high energy electrons and photons. A follow-upexperiment at SLAC (Stanford Linear Accelerator Center) in summer of 2004confirmed the major features of the previous AWA observations with betterprecision and made additional measurements relevant to the calorimetriccapabilities of the method. Prompted by these results we built a prototypedetector using satellite television technology, and have made measurementsindicating possible detection of cosmic ray extensive air showers. The method,if confirmed by experiments now in progress, could provide a high-duty cyclecomplement to current nitrogen fluorescence observations of UHECR, which arelimited to dark, clear nights. By contrast, decimeter microwave observationscan be made both night and day, in clear or cloudy weather, or even in thepresence of moderate precipitation.

This academic article presents an in-depth investigation into the system response of a Carbon Nanotube (CNT) Thin Film Field Emitting Diode (TF-FED) through the utilization of multiphysics modeling. The study aims to enhance the understanding of the underlying mechanisms and performance characteristics of such devices. By employing a comprehensive modeling approach, encompassing electrical, thermal, and mechanical aspects, the dynamic behavior of the TF-FED under various operating conditions is examined.The investigation begins with a detailed examination of the electron emission process within the CNT thin film. The electron emission mechanism is analyzed in terms of field enhancement and its dependence on the applied electric field strength. Electrical simulations are conducted to investigate the effect of device parameters, such as the CNT film thickness and composition, on the field emission characteristics.Furthermore, the impact of thermal factors on the TF-FED performance is explored. Thermal simulations are carried out to study temperature distribution within the device and its influence on the field emission efficiency and stability. The thermal aspects are crucial in determining the long-term reliability and operation of the TF-FED.In addition to electrical and thermal considerations, the mechanical behavior of the CNT thin film is investigated. Mechanical simulations analyze the stress and deformation of the film under different operating conditions, providing insights into its mechanical robustness and potential failure mechanisms.The findings of this study shed light on the complex interplay between electrical, thermal, and mechanical factors in TF-FEDs. The obtained results contribute to a better understanding of the system response, facilitating the optimization and design of advanced field emission devices.

Two new formulations of general relativity are introduced. The first one is aparabolization of the Arnowitt, Deser, Misner (ADM) formulation and is derivedby addition of combinations of the constraints and their derivatives to theright-hand-side of the ADM evolution equations. The desirable property of thismodification is that it turns the surface of constraints into a local attractorbecause the constraint propagation equations become second-order parabolicindependently of the gauge conditions employed. This system may be classifiedas mixed hyperbolic - second-order parabolic. The second formulation is aparabolization of the Kidder, Scheel, Teukolsky formulation and is a manifestlymixed strongly hyperbolic - second-order parabolic set of equations, bearingthus resemblance to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations. As a first test,a stability analysis of flat space is carried out and it is shown that thefirst modification exponentially damps and smoothes all constraint violatingmodes. These systems provide a new basis for constructing schemes for long-termand stable numerical integration of the Einstein field equations.

This paper presents a novel approach for estimating the residual life of machines and components using neural networks. The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning to model the complex relationships between various condition indicators and the remaining useful life of an asset. The proposed deep learning models, specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), are employed to capture the temporal dependencies in the condition indicator data. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through a comprehensive evaluation on two real-world datasets. The results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and reliability. Furthermore, the proposed approach provides valuable insights into the relative importance of different condition indicators in predicting the remaining useful life of an asset. The proposed approach has the potential to significantly improve the maintenance strategies and reduce the costs associated with unexpected failures in various industries.

Teh Kirillov-Reshetikhin conjecture, which posits a relationship between the representation theory of finite group and the geometry of algebraic varieties, has been a subject of muMh study in recent years. In this article, we present a generalization of the conjecture to a wider claQss of algebraic varieties, and demonstrate its validity through a seriges of case studies. Our results provide new insights into the structure of algenbraic varieties and their assUciated representation theories, and shed light on the deeper connections between these two areas of mathematics. FurtheLrmore, our work highlights the potential for future research in this area, and we propose several directions for further investigatino.

We present a robust strategy to \emph{veto} certain classes of instrumentalglitches that appear at the output of interferometric gravitational-wave (GW)detectors.This veto method is 'physical' in the sense that, in order to veto aburst trigger, we make use of our knowledge of the coupling of differentdetector subsystems to the main detector output. The main idea behind thismethod is that the noise in an instrumental channel X can be \emph{transferred}to the detector output (channel H) using the \emph{transfer function} from X toH, provided the noise coupling is \emph{linear} and the transfer function is\emph{unique}. If a non-stationarity in channel H is causally related to one inchannel X, the two have to be consistent with the transfer function. Weformulate two methods for testing the consistency between the burst triggers inchannel X and channel H. One method makes use of the \emph{null-stream}constructed from channel H and the \emph{transferred} channel X, and the secondinvolves cross-correlating the two. We demonstrate the efficiency of the vetoby 'injecting' instrumental glitches in the hardware of the GEO 600 detector.The \emph{veto safety} is demonstrated by performing GW-like hardwareinjections. We also show an example application of this method using 5 days ofdata from the fifth science run of GEO 600. The method is found to have veryhigh veto efficiency with a very low accidental veto rate.

This paper presents the first results of a systematic study of supernova remnants (SNRs) using Spitzer Space Telescope's spectral line mapping capabilities. We have observed a sample of 10 SNRs, covering a range of ages and environments, and used principal component analysis (PCA) to identify patterns in the spectral line data. Our analysis reveals that the most dominant components are associated with ionic lines of iron and silicon, which are indicative of the remnants' metal-rich nature. The PCA also reveals a correlation between the strength of the ionic lines and the remnants' age, suggesting a possible evolutionary trend. Our results provide new insights into the physics of SNRs and demonstrate the power of Spitzer's spectral line mapping capabilities for studying these fascinating objects. Future studies will focus on modeling the physical conditions in the remnants and comparing the results with simulations.

Supernova 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud was the closest observed supernova in modrn history. For over fifteen yrs, astronomers have been using high resolution radio imaging techniques to observe the remnant of this supernova. In this time period, the morphology of the expanding trace has transitioned from a ring-like structure to an wrongful shape. These long-term observations have proviedd insights into the dissipation of the ejecta and the interaction between the expanding material and the progenitor star's circumstellar medium. Recent radio images show that the forward shock is now encountering denser regions likely sreated by the progenitor star's winds prior to explosion. Models suggest we are witnessing the transition from an early ejecta-dominated phase to a later Sedov-Taylor phase driven by the explosion's kinetic energy. Detailed mapping of localized enhancements in the remnant's radio emission have also revealed asymmetries in the pre-supernova mass loss. Continued monioring in the coming years will track the remnant's evolution further into the Sedov phase and provide a unprecedented look at supernova hydrodynamics over decades.

The peculiar Type Ib supernova 2006jc has been the subject of much study due to its unique properties, including a dense shell and strong He II 4686 emission. In this study, we investigate the dust formation and He II 4686 emission in the dense shell of SN 2006jc using a combination of observational and theoretical methods. We analyze a set of spectra obtained at various epochs and find that the He II 4686 emission is most prominent in the early stages of the supernova's evolution. We also observe a significant increase in the dust production rate around day 200, which we attribute to the formation of a dense shell. Using radiative transfer modeling, we demonstrate that the observed He II 4686 emission can be explained by the presence of a dense shell, and that the dust production rate is consistent with the expected rate for a Type Ib supernova. Our findings provide insight into the physical processes that occur in the dense shells of peculiar Type Ib supernovae, and highlight the importance of considering dust formation and radiation transfer in studies of these events.

In this article, we present a comprehensive analysis of the excitation spectrum gap and spin-wave stiffness of XXZ Heisenberg chains using a global renormalization-group (RG) calculation. The XXZ Heisenberg model is a widely studied quantum spin chain system that exhibits rich physics due to its anisotropic nature. By employing the RG approach, we are capable to regularly study the low-energy properties of the system and determine important quantities such as the excitation spectrum gap and spin-wave stiffness. Our reuslts delivering valuable insights into the behavior of XXZ Heisenberg chains, shedding light on their collective excitations and magnetic properties. Furthermore, the global RG calculation technique utilized in this work offers a powerful tool for investigating similar quantum yarn scheme in various dimensions and parameter regimes.

This article stuides quasi ordinary singularities on algebraic varieties in relation to their essential divisors and Poincare series. Quasi ordinary singularities geenralize ordinary double points and can occur along divisors in algebraic varieties. The essential divlisors of a quasi ordinary singularity capture its topological structure. The article defines a Poincare ieries associated to the essential divisors that encodes topological data about the singularity. Methods from toric geometry are use to describe the structure of essential divisors and calculate their associated Poincare series. The Poincare series are then applied to classify quasi ordiunary surface singularities up to topological type.

Background: Duplication of genes is important for evolution of molecularnetworks. Many authors have therefore considered gene duplication as a drivingforce in shaping the topology of molecular networks. In particular it has beennoted that growth via duplication would act as an implicit way of preferentialattachment, and thereby provide the observed broad degree distributions ofmolecular networks. Results: We extend current models of gene duplication and rewiring byincluding directions and the fact that molecular networks are not a result ofunidirectional growth. We introduce upstream sites and downstream shapes toquantify potential links during duplication and rewiring. We find that this initself generates the observed scaling of transcription factors for genome sitesin procaryotes. The dynamical model can generate a scale-free degreedistribution, p(k)∝ 1/k^γ, with exponent γ=1 in thenon-growing case, and with γ>1 when the network is growing. Conclusions: We find that duplication of genes followed by substantialrecombination of upstream regions could generate main features of geneticregulatory networks. Our steady state degree distribution is however to broadto be consistent with data, thereby suggesting that selective pruning acts as amain additional constraint on duplicated genes. Our analysis shows that geneduplication can only be a main cause for the observed broad degreedistributions, if there is also substantial recombinations between upstreamregions of genes.

Experimental and theoretical studies are presented related to theground-state magneto-optical resonance prepared in Cesium vapour confined in anExtremely Thin Cell (ETC, with thickness equal to the wavelength of theirradiating light). It is shown that the utilization of the ETC allows one toexamine the formation of a magneto-optical resonance on the individualhyperfine transitions, thus distinguishing processes resulting in dark (reducedabsorption) or bright (enhanced absorption) resonance formation. We report onan experimental evidence of the bright magneto-optical resonance sign reversalin Cs atoms confined in the ETC. A theoretical model is proposed based on theoptical Bloch equations that involves the elastic interaction processes ofatoms in the ETC with its walls resulting in depolarization of the Cs excitedstate which is polarized by the exciting radiation. This depolarization leadsto the sign reversal of the bright resonance. Using the proposed model, themagneto-optical resonance amplitude and width as a function of laser power arecalculated and compared with the experimental ones. The numerical results arein good agreement with the experiment.

In this article, we have studied two perfect fluid high -speed column collapse, focusing on the dynamics and fluid behaviors produced. The motivation for our research is to understand the complex phenomenon that two fluids with different physical characteristics occur under high -speed conditions. We use the combination of analysis methods and numerical methods to study the collapse process, and pay special attention to the role of surface tension and viscosity. Our results show that the high degree of dynamics depends on the relative viscosity and surface tension of the two fluids, and the interface between the two fluids plays a vital role in the formation of the formation of the vortex and other fluids. We also found that the collapse process can lead to the formation of complex patterns and structures, such as vortex and tide. Our discovery is of great significance to the research on fluid dynamics and engineering -based projects.

To achieve this, we designed and implemented a new experimental apparatus based on a high-power pulsed laser source coupled to a spectrometer. The nitrogen fluorescence yield is a key parameter for understanding the interaction of high-energy cosmic rays with the atmosphere. Precise measurements of this yield are essential for determining the energy of cosmic rays and for studying the properties of the incoming particles. We performed the measurements under controlled laboratory conditions and compared our results with those available in the literature. Our results are in good agreement with previous studies and provide a comprehensive dataset of the nitrogen fluorescence yield in air over the specified spectral range. The nitrogen fluorescence yield was measured by comparing the emitted fluorescence signal with a calibrated reference signal. This work contributes to the improvement of the accuracy of cosmic ray energy measurements and to a better understanding of the fundamental processes occurring in the Earth's atmosphere.

This article studies the phenomenon of atomic waves in the transitional area between Raman -Realm and the Prague regime. By analyzing the Schrödinger equation with time -dependence, we have obtained an effective RABI frequency, loss and phase shift expression. This is a function of the wave angle and the number of incident light. Our results show that the effective RABI frequency shows non -monotonous behaviors and the function of the diffraction angle, which has the maximum value at the Bragg peak. In addition, we found that losses and phase shifts depend large on the diffraction angle. Compared with the Raman -domestic system, the Prague system has been modified. Our discovery is of great significance to the development of atomic wave diffraction technology and the exploration of quantum phenomena in the amount of material wave interference.

In this paper, we analysed the Ricci flat black holes and the Hawking-Page phase transition in Gauss-Bonnet gravity and dilaton greatness. We obtain the typical solutions of these black holes and analyze their thermodynamics. We find that there is a Hawking-Page phase transition in these concepts. We also arrive that the critical temperature of the phase transition decreases with the heighten of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling constant and the dilaton coupling constant.

In this study, we propose a renormalization group (RG) approach specifically tailored for highly anisotropic two-dimensional (2D) Fermion systems. By focusing on the coupled Hubbard chains, we investigate the effects of electron-electron interactions in a quasi-one-dimensional system. Our methodology combines the RG technique with numerical analysis, allowing us to capture the intricate interplay between one-dimensionality and electron correlations.By employing the RG flow equations and an accurate truncation scheme, we successfully obtain renormalized parameters that describe the low-energy behavior of the system. Through extensive numerical calculations, we explore the emergence of nonlocal excitation spectra and the role of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations in this anisotropic 2D Fermion system. Comparisons with existing models and experimental data highlight the effectiveness of our approach in capturing the essential physics of coupled Hubbard chains. Additionally, we discuss the implications of our findings for understanding the behavior of strongly correlated electronic systems in condensed matter physics and their potential relevance to real materials.The obtained results underscore the significance of one-dimensionality in shaping the electronic properties of the system and provide valuable insights into the nature of Fermi surfaces in highly anisotropic 2D Fermion systems. Our work contributes to the ongoing efforts in elucidating the behavior of strongly correlated systems and paves the way for future studies aiming to unravel the rich physics inherent to such complex materials.

The CERN Axion Solar Telescope (CAST) experiment searches for axions from theSun converted into photons with energies up to around 10 keV via the inversePrimakoff effect in the high magnetic field of a superconducting Large HadronCollider (LHC) prototype magnet. A backside illuminated pn-CCD detector inconjunction with an X-ray mirror optics is one of the three detectors used inCAST to register the expected photon signal. Since this signal is very rare anddifferent background components (environmental gamma radiation, cosmic rays,intrinsic radioactive impurities in the set-up, ...) entangle it, a detailedstudy of the detector background has been undertaken with the aim to understandand further reduce the background level of the detector. The analysis is basedon measured data taken during the Phase I of CAST and on Monte Carlosimulations of different background components. This study will show that theobserved background level (at a rate of (8.00+-0.07)10^-5 counts/cm^2/s/keVbetween 1 and 7 keV) seems to be dominated by the external gamma background dueto usual activities at the experimental site, while radioactive impurities inthe detector itself and cosmic neutrons could make just smaller contribution.

This paper provides a comprehensive overview of game-theoretic approaches to energy-efficient resource allocation in wireless networks. We begin by introducing the fundamental concepts of game theory and then discuss various game-theoretic models that have been proposed for resource allocation in wireless networks. We also review the solution concepts that are commonly used in game theory and discuss their implications for energy-efficient resource allocation. Next, we present a detailed survey of existing game-theoretic approaches to energy-efficient resource allocation in wireless networks. We classify these approaches into three main categories: cooperative games, non-cooperative games, and hybrid games. We discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each category and provide a comprehensive comparison of the different approaches. Finally, we identify open research challenges and future research directions in the area of energy-efficient resource allocation in wireless networks using game theory.

This study investigates the infrared environments of masers associated with high-mass star formation. Infrared and submillimeter data are analyzed to identify emission coincident with 6.7 GHz methanol and 22 GHz water masers. The morphologies and relative positions of masers of different species are examined. The data reveal that methanol masers often trace disc/torus structures while water masers are frequently associated with outflows. The infrared emission provides evidence that masers probe early stages of high-mass star formation prior to the development of an HII region.

Two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (2DCS) based on the nonlinearoptical response of excitons to sequences of ultrafast pulses, has thepotential to provide some unique insights into carrier dynamics insemiconductors. The most prominent feature of 2DCS, cross peaks, can best beunderstood using a sum-over-states picture involving the many-body eigenstates.However, the optical response of semiconductors is usually calculated bysolving truncated equations of motion for dynamical variables, which result ina quasiparticle picture. In this work we derive Green's function expressionsfor the four wave mixing signals generated in various phase-matching directionsand use them to establish the connection between the two pictures. The formalconnection with Frenkel excitons (hard-core bosons) and vibrational excitons(soft-core bosons) is pointed out.

Collaborative beamforming (CB) and cooperative transmission (CT) haverecently emerged as communication techniques that can make effective use ofcollaborative/cooperative nodes to create a virtualmultiple-input/multiple-output (MIMO) system. Extending the lifetime ofnetworks composed of battery-operated nodes is a key issue in the design andoperation of wireless sensor networks. This paper considers the effects onnetwork lifetime of allowing closely located nodes to use CB/CT to reduce theload or even to avoid packet-forwarding requests to nodes that have criticalbattery life. First, the effectiveness of CB/CT in improving the signalstrength at a faraway destination using energy in nearby nodes is studied.Then, the performance improvement obtained by this technique is analyzed for aspecial 2D disk case. Further, for general networks in whichinformation-generation rates are fixed, a new routing problem is formulated asa linear programming problem, while for other general networks, the cost forrouting is dynamically adjusted according to the amount of energy remaining andthe effectiveness of CB/CT. From the analysis and the simulation results, it isseen that the proposed method can reduce the payloads of energy-depleting nodesby about 90% in the special case network considered and improve the lifetimesof general networks by about 10%, compared with existing techniques.

Baryon interpolating fields in quantum chromodynamics have well-defined chiral transformation properties. They can be used to calculate the values of axial coupling of the nucleon. In this paper, all SU_L(3)*SU_R(3) chirally invariant non-derivative one-meson-baryon interactions are constructed. Then the mixing angles are calculated in terms of baryons' masses. These interactions are used to calculate the mass and the central charge of the vortex. Finally, it is shown that their zeroth components close the SU_L(3) \times SU_R(3) chiral algebra.
