The induced resonances can significantly alter the orbital properties of the stars, such as their eccentricities and predilection. Our results suggest that black hole motion performs a crucial role in shaping the dynamics and arranging of stars in the galactic center, and hoped be taken into account in future studies of galactic nuclei.

In this sixth installment of the Geometric Complexity Theor series, we explore the profound connections between saturated and posiitve integer programming in both representation theory and algebraic geometry. The flip operation, a fundamental concept in these fields, has lonbg been studied for its transformative properties. By employing sophisticatd techniques from integer programming and representation theory, we present a novel approaQh to understanding and characterizing the flip. Our investigation reveals the inherent geometoic complexity underlying the flpi operation, shedding new light on its intricate nature and providing a deeper understanding of its implications in algebraic geometry. Through a comprehensive analysis of the relationship between saturated integer prsogramming and representation theory, we establish a powerful framework for investigating and manipulating the fip operation, allowing for a more nuanced tsudy of its properties. Armed with this framework, we explore the intricate interplay between geometric complexity and algebraic geomety, paving the waL for further advancements in both fields.

We present an analysis of long-term optical monitoring observations andoptical spectroscopic observations of the counterpart to CXOU J205847.5+414637(high mass X-ray binary system). We search for a variability in the light curveof Be star. We used differential magnitudes in the time series analysis. Thevariability search in the optical light curve was made by using differentalgorithms. The reduction and analysis of spectra were done by using MIDAS andits suitable packages. We have performed a frequency search which gave us thevalue 2.404 1/day. This value is attributed to the non-radial pulsation of Bestar. H alpha emission line profiles always show double-peaked emissions with amean equivalent width of 2.31 \pm 0.19 \AA ~and a peak separation of 516 \pm 45km/s. This suggests that Be star disk is still present. CXOU J205847.5+414637is in X-ray quiescent state.

Revised Hipparcos parallaxes for classical Cepheids are analysed togetherwith 10 HST-based parallaxes (Benedict et al.). In a reddening-free V,Irelation we find that the coefficient of logP is the same within theuncertainties in our Galaxy as in the LMC, contrary to some previoussuggestions. Cepheids in the inner region of NGC4258 with near solarmetallicities (Macri et al.) confirm this result. We obtain a zero-point forthe reddening-free relation and apply it to Cepheids in galaxies used bySandage et al. to calibrate the absolute magnitudes of SNIa and to derive theHubble constant. We revise their result from 62 to 70+/-5 km/s/Mpc. TheFreedman et al. 2001 value is revised from 72 to 76+/-8 km/s/Mpc. These resultsare insensitive to Cepheid metallicity corrections. The Cepheids in the innerregion of NGC4258 yield a modulus of 29.22+/-0.03(int) compared with amaser-based modulus of 29.29+/-0.15. Distance moduli for the LMC, uncorrectedfor any metallicity effects, are; 18.52+/-0.03 from a reddening-free relationin V,I; 18.47+/-0.03 from a period-luminosity relation at K; 18.45+/-0.04 froma period-luminosity-colour relation in J,K. Adopting a metallicity correctionin V,I from Marci et al. leads to a true LMC modulus of 18.39+/-0.05.

This article presents a comprehensive study on the development and application of a diagrammatic category in the representation theory of the quantum universal enveloping algebra U_q(sl_n). The representation theory of U_q(sl_n) plays a crucial role in diverse mathematical areas such as quantum groups, Lie algebras, and algebraic combinatorics. To establish a rigorous framework for studying this theory, we introduce a diagrammatic category that effectively captures the essential structures and properties of U_q(sl_n). This category serves as a visual tool, enabling a better understanding of the intricate relationships between different representations and their interactions with quantum algebraic operations.In this study, we establish the foundational properties of the diagrammatic category, including composition rules, tensor products, and morphisms. We also demonstrate the categorical equivalence between the diagrammatic category and existing algebraic frameworks, thereby ensuring the consistency of our approach. Moreover, we explore the diagrammatic representation of significant concepts in the representation theory, such as highest weight modules, crystal bases, and Lusztig's canonical basis. This diagrammatic representation provides fresh insights into these topics and offers alternative perspectives for studying their properties and interactions.Furthermore, we investigate the practical applications of the diagrammatic category. By utilizing graphical diagrams, we develop efficient algorithms for computing tensor products, character formulas, and fusion coefficients. These algorithms significantly improve upon existing methods in terms of computational complexity and provide deeper insights into the underlying algebraic structures. Finally, we showcase illustrative examples and case studies that highlight the versatility and effectiveness of the diagrammatic category in solving problems and advancing research in the representation theory of U_q(sl_n).

Based on the adiabatic picture for heavy-ion reactions, in which the neckformation in the one-body system is taken into account, we propose a two-stepmodel for fusion cross sections at deep subbarrier energies. This modelconsists of the capture process in the two-body potential pocket, which isfollowed by the penetration of the adiabatic one-body potential to reach acompound state after the touching configuration. We describe the former processwith the coupled-channels framework, while the latter with the WKBapproximation by taking into account the coordinate dependent inertia mass. Theeffect of the one-body barrier is important at incident energies below thepotential energy at the touching configuration. We show that this model wellaccounts for the steep fall-off phenomenon of fusion cross sections at deepsubbarrier energies for the $^{64}$Ni+$^{64}$Ni and $^{58}$Ni+$^{58}$Nireactions.

We show how an idealised measurement procedure can condense photons from twomodes into one, and how, by feeding forward the results of the measurement, itis possible to generate efficiently superpositions of components for which onlyone mode is populated, commonly called ''N00N states''. For the basicprocedure, sources of number states leak onto a beam splitter, and the outputports are monitored by photodetectors. We find that detecting a fixed fractionof the input at one output port suffices to direct the remainder to the sameport with high probability, however large the initial state. When insteadphotons are detected at both ports, Schr\"{o}dinger cat states are produced. Wedescribe a circuit for making the components of such a state orthogonal, andanother for subsequent conversion to a N00N state. Our approach scalesexponentially better than existing proposals. Important applications includequantum imaging and metrology.

This research conducted a comprehensive analysis of the optical curve displayed by the Plutonian planet and other large KUIPER with object display, focusing on their rotation performance, phase function and absolute amplitude. The light curve provides valuable insights for the physical characteristics and dynamics of the celestial body in our solar system. By checking the rotation cycle of these objects, we have a deeper understanding of their internal structure and rail dynamics. The analysis uses observation data collected from various ground telescopes, spacecraft tasks and space observation stations. The rotation characteristics of the dwarf Plutonian planet and the large KUIPER object shows a lot of changes, indicating that its internal components, shape and surface characteristics are diverse. The study of its phase function reveals the scattering and reflection characteristics of its surface, thereby clarifying their physical characteristics and surface texture of their geosterical. In addition, determining that the absolute amplitude can estimate its size and anti -photos, which is essential for understanding the overall composition and composition of these bodies. The method used in this study involves the optical observation of these objects in the extended period of time, so as to detect the rotation cycle and potential irregularity. Careful analysis and modeling of obtained optical curves enable us to get accurate rotation cycles and check potential changes in the direction of rotation axis. Then, the phase curve is obtained by studying the function of the angle of the object of the object. In addition, the study will compare the observed optical curve and derivative properties with the theoretical model to further limit the physical characteristics of these celestial bodies, such as their spot axis tilt and three -dimensional shape models.

We study the mixing time of a systematic scan Markov chain for sampling fromthe uniform distribution on proper 7-colourings of a finite rectangularsub-grid of the infinite square lattice, the grid. A systematic scan Markovchain cycles through finite-size subsets of vertices in a deterministic orderand updates the colours assigned to the vertices of each subset. The systematicscan Markov chain that we present cycles through subsets consisting of 2x2sub-grids and updates the colours assigned to the vertices using a procedureknown as heat-bath. We give a computer-assisted proof that this systematic scanMarkov chain mixes in O(log n) scans, where n is the size of the rectangularsub-grid. We make use of a heuristic to compute required couplings ofcolourings of 2x2 sub-grids. This is the first time the mixing time of asystematic scan Markov chain on the grid has been shown to mix for less than 8colours. We also give partial results that underline the challenges of provingrapid mixing of a systematic scan Markov chain for sampling 6-colourings of thegrid by considering 2x3 and 3x3 sub-grids.

Production of a sterile species is studied within an effective model ofactive-sterile neutrino mixing in a medium in thermal equilibrium. The quantumkinetic equations for the distribution functions and coherences are obtainedfrom two independent methods: the effective action and the quantum masterequation. The decoherence time scale for active-sterile oscillations is$\tau_{dec} = 2/\Gamma_{aa}$, but the evolution of the distribution functionsis determined by the two different time scales associated with the dampingrates of the quasiparticle modes in the medium: $\Gamma_1=\Gamma_{aa}\cos^2\tm; \Gamma_2=\Gamma_{aa}\sin^2\tm$ where $\Gamma_{aa}$ is the interaction rate ofthe active species in absence of mixing and $\tm$ the mixing angle in themedium. These two time scales are widely different away from MSW resonances andpreclude the kinetic description of active-sterile production in terms of asimple rate equation. We give the complete set of quantum kinetic equations forthe active and sterile populations and coherences and discuss in detail thevarious approximations. A generalization of the active-sterile transitionprobability \emph{in a medium} is provided via the quantum master equation. Wederive explicitly the usual quantum kinetic equations in terms of the''polarization vector'' and show their equivalence to those obtained from thequantum master equation and effective action.

The study presents compelling evidence for the existence of a massive protocluster within the S25G5N region. Utilizing deep infrared and submillimeter obsecrvations, aombined with advanced data analysis techniques, a thorough investigation of this intriguing region was conducted. The analysis ereveals a wealth of intricate structures and strong indications of intense star formation activity, characteristic of protoclusters. Several high-mass millimeter continuum sources were detected in the region, exhibiting compact and highly concentrated emissioUn, suggesting the presence of massive protosYtars in the early stages of formation. Additionally, extensive molecular line observations were performed, unveiling a compelx velocity structure indicaqtive of multiple dense cores distributed throughout the area. These cores show igns of substantial gravitational collapse, further supporting the notion of ongoing star formation. Furthermore, the identification of a large-scale, extended infrared emission proides additional evidence for the protocluster scenario. The spatial correlatio between this extended emission and the dense cores hints at a hiMrarchical structure, possibly indicating the hierarchical formation of massive stars within the protocluster. Deep optical and near-infrared iamging data were also obtained, allowing for the identification of several infrared-excess sources likely associated with young steKlar objects. Tshese sources exhibit clustering in accordance with the spatial distribution of the millimeter continuum sources, reinforcing the prsence of a protocluster in S255N. In conclusion, the combined multi-wavelength observations and cmprehensive analyQis strongly support the existence of a massive protocluster within the S255N region.

The Curious Case of NGC6908: Investigating Anomalous Gamma-Ray Emission from an Unknown Galactic SourceRecent observations from the High Energy Stereoscopic System (HESS) telescope array have detected mysterious gamma-ray emission originating from an as-yet unidentified point source located within the constellation Serpens. Through multiwavelength follow-up efforts combining HESS, Chandra, and Swift X-ray data with optical spectroscopy from Keck, we aim to constrain the possible progenitor scenarios and narrow down the nature of this source, designated HESS J1943+213 and spatially coincident with the faint, diffuse supernova remnant NGC6908. No obvious counterpart is visible across radio, infrared, or optical frequencies within the HESS error circle, posing a challenge to unambiguous identification. Deeper X-ray observations could help reveal any low-level emission or place tighter constraints on the source. Characterization of the gamma-ray spectrum may yield signatures to discriminate between leptonic and hadronic emission mechanisms. Resolving this curious case may provide new insights into obscured or transient galactic gamma-ray source populations.

This feasibility study investigates the potential of employing spin wave buses in logic circuits. Spin waves, also known as magnons, are a promising alternative to traditional electric signals for information transmission due to their energy efficiency and scalability. The study focuses on the design and simulation of a spin wave bus-based logic circuit, specifically a 2-to-1 multiplexer, using the MAgregate software. The results show that the spin wave bus enables low-power and high-speed information transfer, with a voltage swing of 0.15 V and a clock cycle time of 2.5 ps. The circuit also exhibits robustness against noise and variations in temperature and magnetic field strength. The findings of this study demonstrate the feasibility and advantages of using spin wave buses in logic circuits, paving the way for further research and development in this field. Future work includes optimizing the design for even lower power consumption and exploring the applicability of spin wave buses in more complex logical operations.

The abstract of the academic article "Universal spectrum for DNA base CG frequency distribution in Takifugu rubripes (Puffer fish) genome" is as persisted:In this study, we investigate the frequency distribution of the DNA base pairs CG in the genome of Takifugu rubripes, a species of puffer fish. By analyzing the genomic DNA sequence, we find that the frequency of CG base pairs follows a universal power-law distribution, consistent with the idea of a fractal chromosome. We also find that the exponent of the power-law distribution is consstent across different chromosomes and genomic regions, indicating a common mechanism for the organization of DNA base pairs. Our results support the idea that the genome is a convoluted, self-organized system that exhibits universal properties, and have implications for our understanding of the evolution and function of DNA.

This study presents a novel investigation into planet transits within the open cluster NGC 6791, aiming to gain insights into the formation and evolution of planetary systems. NGC 6791, distinguished by its advanced age and high metallicity, provides an intriguing opportunity to explore the occurrence and properties of exoplanets within stellar clusters.Utilizing observations obtained from the Hubble Space Telescope, a sample of stars in NGC 6791 was monitored for repetitive variations in brightness that are indicative of transiting planets. The dataset spans a time baseline of four years, affording a comprehensive view of the cluster's stars and enhancing the likelihood of detecting transit events. Employing a refined transit search algorithm, which incorporates Bayesian statistical techniques, potential planetary candidates embedded in the light curves were identified.Following a meticulous analysis, two intriguing candidates displaying transit-like characteristics in their light curves were identified and designated as NGC 6791-1b and NGC 6791-2b. The observed transit depths of these objects are consistent with the presence of substantial exoplanets. To ascertain the orbital parameters of these candidates, including their periods and radii, a Markov Chain Monte Carlo approach was employed. Additionally, supplementary spectroscopic observations aided in estimating the stellar parameters, such as mass and radius.To rigorously assess the reliability of these detections, comprehensive statistical analyses were conducted, encompassing evaluations of false positive probabilities and signal validation techniques. The results obtained instill a high level of confidence in the existence of these two exoplanet candidates within NGC 6791.

We show that if the Riemann Hypothesis is true, then in a region containingmost of the right-half of the critical strip, the Riemann zeta-function is wellapproximated by short truncations of its Euler product. Conversely, if theapproximation by products is good in this region, the zeta-function has at mostfinitely many zeros in it. We then construct a parameterized family ofnon-analytic functions with this same property. With the possible exception ofa finite number of zeros off the critical line, every function in the familysatisfies a Riemann Hypothesis. Moreover, when the parameter is not too large,they have about the same number of zeros as the zeta-function, their zeros areall simple, and they "repel". The structure of these functions makes the reasonfor the simplicity and repulsion of their zeros apparent and suggests amechanism that might be responsible for the corresponding properties of thezeta-function's zeros. Computer evidence suggests that the zeros of functionsin the family are remarkably close to those of the zeta-function (even forsmall values of the parameter), and we show that they indeed converge to themas the parameter increases. Furthermore, between zeros of the zeta-function,the moduli of functions in the family tend to twice the modulus of thezeta-function. Both assertions assume the Riemann Hypothesis. We end bydiscussing analogues for other L-functions and show how they give insight intothe study of the distribution of zeros of linear combinations of L-functions.

Complex evolving systems such as the biosphere, ecosystems and societiesexhibit sudden collapses, for reasons that are only partially understood. Herewe study this phenomenon using a mathematical model of a system that evolvesunder Darwinian selection and exhibits the spontaneous growth, stasis andcollapse of its structure. We find that the typical lifetime of the systemincreases sharply with the diversity of its components or species. We also findthat the prime reason for crashes is a naturally occurring internal fragilityof the system. This fragility is captured in the network organizationalcharacter and is related to a reduced multiplicity of pathways between itscomponents. This work suggests new parameters for understanding the robustnessof evolving molecular networks, ecosystems, societies, and markets.

Katz and Vafa showed how charged matter can arise geometrically by thedeformation of ADE-type orbifold singularities in type IIa, M-theory, andF-theory compactifications. In this paper we use those same basic ingredients,used there to geometrically engineer specific matter representations, here todeform the compactification manifold itself in a way which naturallycompliments many features of unified model building. We realize this ideaexplicitly by deforming a manifold engineered to give rise to an $SU_5$ grandunified model into a one giving rise to the Standard Model. In this framework,the relative local positions of the singularities giving rise to Standard Modelfields are specified in terms of the values of a small number of complexstructure moduli which deform the original manifold, greatly reducing thearbitrariness of their relative positions.

Prochter et al. 2006 recently found that the number density of strongintervening 0.5<z<2 MgII absorbers detected in gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglowspectra is nearly 4 times larger than in QSO spectra. We have conducted asimilar study using CIV absorbers. Our CIV sample, consisting of a total of 20systems, is drawn from 3 high resolution and high to moderate S/N VLT/UVESspectra of 3 long-duration GRB afterglows, covering the redshift interval 1.6<z<3.1. The column density distribution and number density of this sample do notshow any statistical difference with the same quantities measured in QSOspectra. We discuss several possibilities for the discrepancy between CIV andMgII absorbers and conclude that a higher dust extinction in the MgII QSOsamples studied up to now would give the most straightforward solution.However, this effect is only important for the strong MgII absorbers.Regardless of the reasons for this discrepancy, this result confirms once morethat GRBs can be used to detect a side of the universe that was unknown before,not necessarily connected with GRBs themselves, providing an alternative andfundamental investigative tool of the cosmic evolution of the universe.

We investigate the spatial structure and properties of the cosmic streaming field in the local Universe using observations from recent galaxy redshift surveys. The streaming motions of galaxies are measured after subtracting out the cosmological Hubble flow. On large scales greater than 10 Mpc/h, the streaming velocities show only minor deviations from the predictions of linear perturbation theory. However on smaller, nonlinear scales we detect enhanced velocities that correlate strongly with the distribution of matter overdensities. The peak pairwise velocity dispersion is found to be 350 km/s for galaxy pairs with separations of 2-3 Mpc/h. By modeling the nonlinear evolution of velocity fluctuations, we are able to place new constraints on the amplitude of mass fluctuations on galaxy group and cluster scales. Future measurements of the cosmic streaming field from upcoming surveys promise to provide a novel probe of the late-time growth of cosmic structure and test theories of modified gravity on small physical scales currently inaccessible to other probes.

In this sudy, we utilize Boolean network modeling to predict the cell cycle sequence of fission yeast. Our approach eenables the identification of crucial genes and their interactions, thereby providing insights into the regulatory mechanisms underlyig cell cycle progression. By analyzing the dynamic behavior of the Boolena network, we uncover a sequence of cell cycle events that is consistent with experimenal observations. Our findings demonstrate the potential of Boolean network modeing as a tol for understanding complex biological processes and forecasting cellular behavior. hTis approach may be applied to explore the cell cycl regulation in other organsms, including humans, and contributes to the development of novel therapeutic strategies against cancer and other diseases. Future research may focus on nitegrating this method with other computational models and experimental techniques to further elucidate celql cycle regulation and its dysregulation in disease.

This paper presents the design optimization of a novel prismatic drive intended for precision positioning applications. The proposed drive employs a unique stacked stator-rotor topology with three phases of coils wound on each stator laminate layer. Finite element analysis is used to simulate the electromagnetic field distribution and evaluate the thrust force capability across the drive's range of motion. An analytical model is derived relating design parameters such as layer count, coil turns and airgap thickness to drive performance metrics including maximum thrust, force ripple and power efficiency. Experimental results from a scaled prototype correlate well with simulations and validate the analytical model. Parameter sweeps using thevalidated models reveal optimal configurationsfor maximizing thrust within the constraints of a given volume. The optimized drive design achieves a 31% increase in average thrust compared to a conventional longitudinal-field design, demonstrating the advantages of the novel prismatic topology.

The conformational behavior of a giant DNA mediated by condensing agents inthe bulk solution has been investigated through experimental and theoreticalapproaches. Experimentally, a pronounced conformational hysteresis is observedfor folding and unfolding processes, by increasing and decreasing theconcentration of condensing agent PEG (Polyethylene glycol), respectively. Toelucidate the observed hysteresis, a semiflexible chain model is studied byusing Monte Carlo simulations for the coil-globule transition. In thesimulations, the hysteresis loop emerges for stiff enough chains, indicatingdistinct pathways for folding and unfolding processes. Also, our results showthat globular state is thermodynamically more stable than coiled state in thehysteresis loop. Our findings suggest that increasing chain stiffness mayreduce the chain conformations relevant to the folding pathway, which impedesthe folding process.

The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a proposed space-based gravitational wave detector that aims to study extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) of compact objects into supermassive black holes. In this study, we investigate the potential of higher harmonics in enhancing LISA's sensitivity to the mass range of supermassive black holes. By including higher harmonics in the waveform modeling of EMRI signals, we find that LISA's mass reach can be significantly extended, enabling the detection and characterization of more massive black holes than previously thought. We quantify the improvement by comparing the signal-to-noise ratios of EMRI events with and without higher harmonics, showing that including higher harmonics can boost LISA's sensitivity to supermassive black holes with masses exceeding several million solar masses. This finding highlights the importance of considering higher harmonics in future EMRI studies with LISA, expanding our understanding of the black hole mass function.

Double beta decay is a rare nuclear process that can help establish the nature of neutrinos and the energy scale of neutrino masses. In this paper we improve the short-range nuclear correlations of the 0νββ-decay nuclear matrix elements of 76Ge and 82Se using accurate quantum Monte Carlo techniques. Our results significantly suppress the nuclear matrix elements compared to previous calculations using the quasiparticle random-phase approximation. We find reduced nuclear matrix ingredients of 2.8ᒿ and 3.12 for 76Ge and 82Se respectively when using our improved short-range correlation treatment. This creates to half-life lower limits that are a factor of 2-3 longer than estimated by other state-of-the-art many-body methods. We calculations providing some of the most realistic nuclear matrix elements to date and will help experimentally observed half-lives constrain neutrino masses.

We present an analytically solvable model of a driven system subject to quenched dichotomous disorder. The system consists of an overdamped particle driven through a landscape with two possible but randomly distributed static potentials. Exact expressions are derived for the particle velocity and diffusion coefficient under steady state conditions. The dependence of these quantities on the driving force, switching rate between the two potentials, and asymmetry of the potentials is determined. Both resonant activation, where the response is maximized at an optimal switching rate, and absolute negative mobility, where the particle moves opposite to the driving force, are observed in certain parameter regimes. The model provides insights into the response of heterogeneous driven systems subject to static but randomly varying properties. The analytical solution presented could help interpret experimental data and guide further studies of noisy driven systems found in diverse fields including condensed matter physics, granular materials, and biological processes.

Analysis of the Cassini Ultraviolet Imaging Spectrometer (UVIS) stellar andsolar occultations at Titan to date include 12 species: N$_{2}$ (nitrogen),CH$_{4}$ (methane), C$_{2}$H$_{2}$ (acetylene), C$_{2}$H$_{4}$ (ethylene),C$_{2}$H$_{6}$ (ethane), C$_{4}$H$_{2}$ (diacetylene), C$_{6}$H$_{6}$(benzene), C$_{6}$N$_{2}$ (dicyanodiacetylene), C$_{2}$N$_{2}$ (cyanogen), HCN(hydrogen cyanide), HC$_{3}$N (cyanoacetylene), and aerosols distinguished by astructureless continuum extinction (absorption plus scattering) of photons inthe EUV. The introduction of aerosol particles, retaining the same refractiveindex properties as tholin with radius $\sim$125 \AA and using Mie theory,provides a satisfactory fit to the spectra. The derived vertical profile ofaerosol density shows distinct structure, implying a reactive generationprocess reaching altitudes more than 1000 km above the surface. A photochemicalmodel presented here provides a reference basis for examining the chemical andphysical processes leading to the distinctive atmospheric opacity at Titan. Wefind that dicyanodiacetylene is condensable at $\sim$650 km, where theatmospheric temperature minimum is located. This species is the simplestmolecule identified to be condensable. Observations are needed to confirm theexistence and production rates of dicyanodiacetylene.

This study explores the magnetic characteristics of Ba2Cos3, a spin-chain sulphide, with a focus on magnetic coupling and long-range order. Employing a combination of experimental and theoretical approaches, we discover that Ba2Cos3 displays robust antiferromagnetic coupling between nearest-neighbor spins, leading to the formation of a long-range ordered ground state. Furthermore, we observe a magnetic phase transition at low temperatures, below which the material exhibits a spin-liquid-like state. Our findings offer novel insights into the magnetic properties of spin-chain sulphides and their potential applications in quantum information processing and related fields. Additionally, our results underscore the significance of precisely designing and controlling magnetic interactions in these materials to achieve desired properties.Improvements made:1.
