However, the long -term evolution of magnetic turbulence in this environment is still uncertain. In this theoretical study, we use the simulation of the particle in the particle to study the evolution of magnetic turbulence of the electronic choroid plasma characteristics of the theory of relativity without collisions. The simulation shows that as the plasma is the same as the same sex and calories, the magnetic turbulence is effectively generated during the initial impact crossing process. At a longer time scale, the turbulence was gradually declining due to the movement of kinetic energy to micro -plasma waves. This attenuation occurs at the initial turbulence power on the scale of the ion skin. The rate of attenuation depends on the initial turbulence intensity, and the initial initial attenuation is faster. Our results show that the magnetic field is rapidly saturated through the unstable chip, and the continuous non -thermal particles acceleration may require continuously drive the turbulence after impact. The long -term evolution of the magnetic turbulence revealed in this work provides new insights to the granular energy in the physical impact of non -collision -free celestial bodies.

We present an one-dimensional particle-in-cell Monte-Carlo model forcapacitively coupled radio-frequency discharges in oxygen. The modelquantitatively describes the central part of the discharge. For a given voltageand pressure, it self-consistently determines the electric potential and thedistribution functions for electrons, negatively charged atomic oxygen, andpositively charged molecular oxygen. Previously used collision cross sectionsare critically assessed and in some cases modified. Provided associativedetachment due to metastable oxygen molecules is included in the model, theelectro-negativities in the center of the discharge are in excellent agreementwith experiments. Due to lack of empirical data for the cross section of thisprocess, we propose a simple model and discuss its limitations.

We present a new, detailed analysis of late-time mid-infrared (IR)observations of the Type II-P supernova (SN) 2003gd. At about 16 months afterthe explosion, the mid-IR flux is consistent with emission from 4 x 10^(-5)M(solar) of newly condensed dust in the ejecta. At 22 months emission frompoint-like sources close to the SN position was detected at 8 microns and 24microns. By 42 months the 24 micron flux had faded. Considerations ofluminosity and source size rule out the ejecta of SN 2003gd as the main originof the emission at 22 months. A possible alternative explanation for theemission at this later epoch is an IR echo from pre-existing circumstellar orinterstellar dust. We conclude that, contrary to the claim of Sugerman et al.(2006, Science, 313, 196), the mid-IR emission from SN 2003gd does not supportthe presence of 0.02 M(solar) of newly formed dust in the ejecta. There is, asyet, no direct evidence that core-collapse supernovae are major dust factories.

The large cross-sections for top quark pair production at hadron colliders allow precise measurements of the mass of the top quark and differential distributions sensitive to the couplings of the top quark to other particles. These measurements are stringent tests of the Standard Model and can be used to probe the existence of physics beyond the Standard Model. In this paper we study the production of heavy spin-one particles X which couple to the top quark via an effective interaction. We set limits on the couplings of these particles to the top quark using differential distributions measured at the Tevatron and LHC. Our results are competitive with direct searches for X particles decaying to third generation quarks and complement the results of direct searches at the LHC. We compare our results with those obtained assuming top quark pair production via an effective four-quark interaction and find that the two scenarios can be distinguished by the distributions of the transverse momentum of the top quark. We emphasize the importance of including NLO QCD corrections to the signal and background processes in order to obtain reliable exclusion limits on the model parameters.

We study the magnetotransport in small hybrid junctions formed byhigh-mobility GaInAs/InP heterostructures coupled to superconducting (S) andnormal metal (N) terminals. Highly transmissive superconducting contacts to atwo-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) located in a GaInAs/InP heterostructure arerealized by using a Au/NbN layer system. The magnetoresistance of the S/2DEG/Nstructures is studied as a function of dc bias current and temperature. At biascurrents below a critical value, the resistance of the S/2DEG/N structuresdevelops a strong oscillatory dependence on the magnetic field, with anamplitude of the oscillations considerably larger than that of the referenceN/2DEG/N structures. The experimental results are qualitatively explained bytaking Andreev reflection in high magnetic fields into account.

In this article, we explore the properties of spherically symmetric spacetimes in f(R) gravity theories. We examine the Einstein field equations in the Jordan frame and the Einstein-Maxwell equations in the Einstein frame, and discuss the existence of black hole solutions. We also investigate the stability of these solutions and their implications for the viability of f(R) gravity theories. Our findings shed light on the nature of gravitational interactions in these theories and provide new insights into the behavior of matter and energy in strong gravity regimes. Ultimately, our results highlight the importance of considering spherical symmetry in the study of f(R) gravity theories and their potential applications in astrophysics and cosmology.

AIMS: We investigate whether the morphology of bilateral supernova remnants(BSNRs) observed in the radio band is determined mainly either by a non-uniforminterstellar medium (ISM) or by a non-uniform ambient magnetic field. METHODS: We perform 3-D MHD simulations of a spherical SNR shock propagatingthrough a magnetized ISM. Two cases of shock propagation are considered: 1)through a gradient of ambient density with a uniform ambient magnetic field; 2)through a homogeneous medium with a gradient of ambient magnetic fieldstrength. From the simulations, we synthesize the synchrotron radio emission,making different assumptions about the details of acceleration and injection ofrelativistic electrons. RESULTS: We find that asymmetric BSNRs are produced if the line-of-sight isnot aligned with the gradient of ambient plasma density or with the gradient ofambient magnetic field strength. We derive useful parameters to quantify thedegree of asymmetry of the remnants that may provide a powerful diagnostic ofthe microphysics of strong shock waves through the comparison between modelsand observations. CONCLUSIONS: BSNRs with two radio limbs of different brightness can beexplained if a gradient of ambient density or, most likely, of ambient magneticfield strength is perpendicular to the radio limbs. BSNRs with convergingsimilar radio arcs can be explained if the gradient runs between the two arcs.

In this article, we explore the connection between Donaldson theory and non-Kählerian surfaces, particularly those with a second Betti number of 1 (class VII surfaces) and $b_2=1$. We begin by examining the fundamental principles of Donaldson theory and its role in understanding the geometry of non-Kählerian surfaces. We then delve into the specifics of class VII surfaces and their unique properties, which allow for a richer understanding of the interplay between Donaldson theory and these surfaces. Through a combination of mathematical analysis and theoretical exploration, we uncover new insights into the relationship between these two areas of mathematics and reveal the ways in which they shed light on each other. Ultimately, our results provide a deeper understanding of the intricate connections between different areas of geometry and topology, and open up new avenues for future research.

We calculate the tunneling conductance of a graphene normalmetal-insulator-superconductor (NIS) junction with a barrier of thickness $d$and with an arbitrary voltage $V_0$ applied across the barrier region. Wedemonstrate that the tunneling conductance of such a NIS junction is anoscillatory function of both $d$ and $V_0$. We also show that the periodicityand amplitude of such oscillations deviate from their universal values in thethin barrier limit as obtained in earlier work [Phys. Rev. Lett. {\bf 97},217001 (2006)] and become a function of the applied voltage $V_0$. Our resultsreproduces the earlier results on tunneling conductance of such junctions inthe thin [Phys. Rev. Lett. {\bf 97}, 217001 (2006)] and zero [Phys. Rev. Lett.{\bf 97}, 067007 (2006)] barrier limits as special limiting cases. We discussexperimental relevance of our results.

A generalization of Stillinger-Lovett sum rules for three-dimensional jellium derived by Ichimaru et al. is presented in two-dimensional jllium in this paper. The sum rules are deri ved for the two-dimensional electron liquid under the local-field correction within the framework of the density functional theory and connect the phase shifts of the scattered electron waves by an external potential with the characteristics of the fixed local field and density response functions. The generalized sum rules can be used to check the accuracy of apprximate theories for inhomogeneous electron systems. The results are applied to the uniform electron gas and the finite jellium disk as two typical e×amples. The widespread sum rules for the two-dimensional electron liquid are expected to be very useful in studying the properties of inhomogeneous two-dimensional electron systems, such as quantum dotted, metal clusters, and surfaces.

We study theoretically the properties of two Bose-Einstein condensates indifferent spin states, represented by a double Fock state. Individualmeasurements of the spins of the particles are performed in transversedirections, giving access to the relative phase of the condensates. Initially,this phase is completely undefined, and the first measurements provide randomresults. But a fixed value of this phase rapidly emerges under the effect ofthe successive quantum measurements, giving rise to a quasi-classical situationwhere all spins have parallel transverse orientations. If the number ofmeasurements reaches its maximum (the number of particles), quantum effectsshow up again, giving rise to violations of Bell type inequalities. Theviolation of BCHSH inequalities with an arbitrarily large number of spins maybe comparable (or even equal) to that obtained with two spins.

In this study, we present infrared (IR) observations of the galaxy cluster MS 1054-03 to investigate the star formation activity and its evolution within rich galaxy clusters. By analyzing the IR spectral energy distributions of a sample of star-forming galaxies within MS 1054-03, we aim to understand the mechanisms that govern star formation in such extreme environments. Our analysis reveals a diverse distribution of star formation rates (SFRs) among the galaxies, with a significant population of actively star-forming systems. We employ various SFR tracers, including the infrared luminosity and the equivalent width of Hα emission, to estimate the star formation activity within the cluster. Furthermore, we investigate the spatial distribution of star formation within MS 1054-03 and find evidence of environmental effects on the star formation process. Our results indicate a higher concentration of star-forming galaxies near the cluster center, suggesting the influence of strong gravitational interactions and intergalactic gas density. Additionally, we examine the impact of the cluster environment on the evolution of star-forming regions by studying the properties of embedded massive stars, protostars, and ultra-compact HII (UCHII) regions. Moreover, we investigate the role of the intracluster medium (ICM) in regulating the star formation activity by studying the relation between the properties of the gas and the observed SFRs. Our analysis includes the examination of virialized C18O cores and their connection to the star formation process. Finally, we compare our findings in MS 1054-03 with other rich galaxy clusters to deepen our understanding of the interplay between galaxy cluster environments and star formation. Our results contribute to the broader knowledge of star formation mechanisms and their evolution in the context of rich galaxy clusters.

We give a new separability criterion, a necessary condition for separabilityof $N$-partite quantum states. The criterion is based on the Blochrepresentation of a $N$-partite quantum state and makes use of multilinearalgebra, in particular, the matrization of tensors. Our criterion applies to{\it arbitrary} $N$-partite quantum states in$\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}^{d_1}\otimes \mathcal{H}^{d_2} \otimes ... \otimes\mathcal{H}^{d_N}.$ The criterion can test whether a $N$-partite state isentangled and can be applied to different partitions of the $N$-partite system.We provide examples that show the ability of this criterion to detectentanglement. We show that this criterion can detect bound entangled states. Weprove a sufficiency condition for separability of a 3-partite state,straightforwardly generalizable to the case $N > 3,$ under certain condition.We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for separability of a classof $N$-qubit states which includes $N$-qubit PPT states.

Super-Earths, exoplanets with asses between 1-10 Earth masses, are some of the most frequently detected exoplanets. However, characterizing the bulk properties of these distan worlds remains challenging given our limited observatioanl data of planets outside our solar system. This study develops detailed interior structure and composition models of super-Earths to better understgand what physical and geochemical insights can be obtained from various observational measuremeCnts. The models explore a ide parameter space of planet masses, radii, core sizes, mantle compositions and atmospheric properties. The results indicate that measurements of a super-Earth's mass and radius can constrain its bulk composition and differentiation history but provide limited information about the Qproperties of its core, matnle or atmosphere individualqly. Integrating additional observables such as measurement of a planet's atmospheric properties or gravitatioual moQments may help refine interior structure models but substantial uncertainties are likely to remain. Further progress in super-Earth characterization will rely on modeling efforts combiPned with observations from next-generation telescopes.

Let $(\cX, \rho)$ be a discrete metric space. We suppose that the group$\sZ^n$ acts freely on $X$ and that the number of orbits of $X$ with respect tothis action is finite. Then we call $X$ a $\sZ^n$-periodic discrete metricspace. We examine the Fredholm property and essential spectra of band-dominatedoperators on $l^p(X)$ where $X$ is a $\sZ^n$-periodic discrete metric space.Our approach is based on the theory of band-dominated operators on $\sZ^n$ andtheir limit operators. In case $X$ is the set of vertices of a combinatorial graph, the graphstructure defines a Schr\"{o}dinger operator on $l^p(X)$ in a natural way. Weillustrate our approach by determining the essential spectra of Schr\"{o}dingeroperators with slowly oscillating potential both on zig-zag and on hexagonalgraphs, the latter being related to nano-structures.

We study the effects of different forms of information feedback associatedwith mass media on an agent-agent based model of the dynamics of culturaldissemination. In addition to some processes previously considered, we alsoexamine a model of local mass media influence in cultural dynamics. Twomechanisms of information feedback are investigated: (i) direct mass mediainfluence, where local or global mass media act as an additional element in thenetwork of interactions of each agent, and (ii) indirect mass media influence,where global media acts as a filter of the influence of the existing network ofinteractions of each agent. Our results generalize previous findings showingthat cultural diversity builds-up by increasing the strength of the mass mediainfluence. We find that this occurs independently of the mechanisms of action(direct or indirect) of the mass media message. However, through an analysis ofthe full range of parameters measuring cultural diversity, we establish thatthe enhancement of cultural diversity produced by interaction with mass mediaonly occurs for strong enough mass media messages. In comparison with previousstudies a main different result is that weak mass media messages, incombination with agent-agent interaction, are efficient in producing culturalhomogeneity. Moreover, the homogenizing effect of weak mass media messages aremore efficient for direct local mass media messages than for global mass mediamessages or indirect global mass media influences.

A coupling between a light scalar field and neutrinos has been widelydiscussed as a mechanism for linking (time varying) neutrino masses and thepresent energy density and equation of state of dark energy. However, it hasbeen pointed out that the viability of this scenario in the non-relativisticneutrino regime is threatened by the strong growth of hydrodynamicperturbations associated with a negative adiabatic sound speed squared. In thispaper we revisit the stability issue in the framework of linear perturbationtheory in a model independent way. The criterion for the stability of a modelis translated into a constraint on the scalar-neutrino coupling, which dependson the ratio of the energy densities in neutrinos and cold dark matter. Weillustrate our results by providing meaningful examples both for stable andunstable models.

This study examines the correlated modulation observed between the redshifted Fe K alpha line and the continuum emission in the active galactic nucleus (AGN) NGC 3783. Using long-term monitoring data obtained from X-ray observations, we perform a detailed analysis to investigate the connection between these two spectral features. Our results reveal a strong correlation between the variability of the redshifted Fe K alpha line and the continuum emission, indicating a common underlying physical mechanism. We further explore the possible causes of this correlation, considering scenarios such as changes in the accretion rate, variations in the ionization state of the accretion disk, and the presence of strong magnetic fields. Additionally, we examine the implications of our findings on the understanding of AGN accretion processes and the nature of the central supermassive black hole. The observed correlation suggests a complex interplay between the accretion disk and the surrounding environment, providing valuable insights into the accretion processes and feedback mechanisms in AGNs.

This article presents a novel type of neural network architecture that incorporates transient state dynamics. The proposed model uses fading memory units to replace standard activation functions, allowing information from previous time steps to gradually decay over time. Simulation results demonstrate that these "transient state" networks can learn sequential patterns and time-series data more effectively than equivalent feedforward and recurrent neural networks. By more accurately modeling the transient nature of biological neural dynamics, this network architecture may lead to improved performance on tasks involving sequential data and temporal patterns.

In a sensor network, in practice, the communication among sensors is subjectto:(1) errors or failures at random times; (3) costs; and(2) constraints sincesensors and networks operate under scarce resources, such as power, data rate,or communication. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is usually a main factor indetermining the probability of error (or of communication failure) in a link.These probabilities are then a proxy for the SNR under which the links operate.The paper studies the problem of designing the topology, i.e., assigning theprobabilities of reliable communication among sensors (or of link failures) tomaximize the rate of convergence of average consensus, when the linkcommunication costs are taken into account, and there is an overallcommunication budget constraint. To consider this problem, we address a numberof preliminary issues: (1) model the network as a random topology; (2)establish necessary and sufficient conditions for mean square sense (mss) andalmost sure (a.s.) convergence of average consensus when network links fail;and, in particular, (3) show that a necessary and sufficient condition for bothmss and a.s. convergence is for the algebraic connectivity of the mean graphdescribing the network topology to be strictly positive. With these results, weformulate topology design, subject to random link failures and to acommunication cost constraint, as a constrained convex optimization problem towhich we apply semidefinite programming techniques. We show by an extensivenumerical study that the optimal design improves significantly the convergencespeed of the consensus algorithm and can achieve the asymptotic performance ofa non-random network at a fraction of the communication cost.

In this paper, we consider a multi-antenna broadcast channel (BC) with multiple transmitters and receivers, where each transmitter is equipped with multiple antennas and each receiver is equipped with a single antenna. We study the problem of determining the optimal number of users that should be turned on in the BC in order to maximize the sum-rate capacity. We first consider the case where the channel state information is perfectly known at the transmitters and receivers. For this case, we propose an optimal algorithm for determining the optimal number of users to turn on. We then consider the case where the channel state information is not perfectly known at the transmitters and receivers. For this case, we propose a heuristic algorithm for determining the optimal number of users to turn on. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithms can significantly improve the sum-rate capacity of the BC.

This article delves into the application of duality theory in understanding representations of Baumslag-Solitar groups, a fundamental concept in combinatorial group theory with far-reaching implications in mathematics and computer science. The author introduces a novel approach to analyzing the representations of these groups, shedding light on their structure and properties. The article meticulously examines the duality between the representations of Baumslag-Solitar groups and their commutator subgroups, offering a fresh perspective on the subject. The author demonstrates the versatility of the duality approach by using it to construct novel representations of Baumslag-Solitar groups and investigate their properties. This work makes a significant contribution to the fields of combinatorial group theory and representation theory, opening up new avenues for future research. The results and techniques presented in the article are accessible to researchers and graduate students in mathematics and computer science, and they have the potential to inspire new applications and advancements in the field.

This article introduces the observation results of the three external TRE-2 transferred as part of the transit light curve project. The transfer was observed with a small telescope network. The collected data showed the size and track of the planet, and its accuracy was unprecedented. The result provides valuable insights for the atmospheric characteristics of the earth and proves that the power of small observations is in external system research. The data obtained during the transition period has been combined with existing data, thinking that the earth generates exquisite embryos, which will help future research on TRE-2. The study also emphasizes the major progress made in the field of external planet science through the use of small telescope and innovative observation strategies.

Within the internal shock scenario we consider different mechanisms of highenergy ($>1$ MeV) photon production inside a Gamma Ray Burst (GRB) fireball andderive the expected high energy photon spectra from individual GRBs during theprompt phase. The photon spectra of leptonic and hadronic origins are comparedwithin different sets of parameter regimes. Our results suggest that the highenergy emission is dominated by the leptonic component if fraction of shockenergy carried by electrons is not very small (e.g. $\epsilon_e > 10^{-3}$).For very small values of $\epsilon_e$ the hadronic emission component could becomparable to or even exceed the leptonic component in the GeV-TeV regime.However, in this case a much larger energy budget of the fireball is requiredto account for the same level of the observed sub-MeV spectrum. The fireballsare therefore extremely inefficient in radiation. For a canonical fireball bulkLorentz factor (e.g. $\Gamma=400$), emissions above $\sim 10$ GeV areattenuated by two-photon pair production processes. For a fireball with an evenhigher Lorentz factor, the cutoff energy is higher, and emissions of 10 TeV -PeV due to $\pi^0$-decay can also escape from the internal shocks. The fluxlevel is however too low to be detected by current TeV detectors, and thesephotons also suffer attenuation by external soft photons.

We present deep emission-line imaging taken with the SOAR Optical ImagingCamera of the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) in the nearby (z=0.035) X-raycluster 2A0335+096. We analyze long-slit optical spectroscopy, archival VLA,Chandra X-ray, and XMM UV data. 2A0335+096 is a bright, cool-core X-raycluster, once known as a cooling flow. Within the highly disturbed corerevealed by Chandra X-ray observations, 2A0335+096 hosts a highly structuredoptical emission-line system. The redshift of the companion is within 100 km/sof the BCG and has certainly interacted with the BCG, and is likely bound toit. The comparison of optical and radio images shows curved filaments inH-alpha emission surrounding the resolved radio source. The velocity structureof the emission-line bar between the BCG nucleus and the companion galaxyprovides strong evidence for an interaction between the two in the last ~50Myrs. The age of the radio source is similar to the interaction time, so thisinteraction may have provoked an episode of radio activity. We estimate a starformation rate of >7 solar mass/yr based on the Halpha and archival UV data, arate similar to, but somewhat lower than, the revised X-ray cooling rate of10-30 solar masses/year estimated from XMM spectra by Peterson & workers. TheHalpha nebula is limited to a region of high X-ray surface brightness and coolX-ray temperature. The detailed structures of H-alpha and X-ray gas differ. Thepeak of the X-ray emission is not the peak of H-alpha emission, nor does it liein the BCG. The estimated age of the radio lobes and their interaction with theoptical emission-line gas, the estimated timescale for depletion andaccumulation of cold gas, and the dynamical time in the system are all similar,suggesting a common trigger mechanism.

This paper proposes a method to address the longstanding problem of lack ofmonotonicity in estimation of conditional and structural quantile functions,also known as the quantile crossing problem. The method consists in sorting ormonotone rearranging the original estimated non-monotone curve into a monotonerearranged curve. We show that the rearranged curve is closer to the truequantile curve in finite samples than the original curve, establish afunctional delta method for rearrangement-related operators, and derivefunctional limit theory for the entire rearranged curve and its functionals. Wealso establish validity of the bootstrap for estimating the limit law of thethe entire rearranged curve and its functionals. Our limit results are genericin that they apply to every estimator of a monotone econometric function,provided that the estimator satisfies a functional central limit theorem andthe function satisfies some smoothness conditions. Consequently, our resultsapply to estimation of other econometric functions with monotonicityrestrictions, such as demand, production, distribution, and structuraldistribution functions. We illustrate the results with an application toestimation of structural quantile functions using data on Vietnam veteranstatus and earnings.

(Conext:) Surveys of Wolf-Rayet (WR) populations in nearby galaxies providetests of evolutionary models plus Type Ib/c supernova progenitors. Thisspectroscopic study complements the recent imaging survey of the spiral galaxyNGC 300 by Schild et al. (Aims): Revisions to the known WR content of NGC 300are presented. We investigate the WR nature of candidate #41 from Schild et al.which is spatially coincident with the bright X-ray point source NGC 300 X-1;(Methods:) VLT/FORS2 multi-object spectroscopy of WR candidates in NGC 300 isobtained; (Results:) We establish an early-type WN nature of #41, i.e. similarto the optical counterpart of IC 10 X-1, which closely resembles NGC 300 X-1.We confirm 9 new WR stars, bringing the current WR census of the inner disk to31, with N(WC)/N(WN)~0.9. (Conclusions:) If #41 is the optical counterpart forNGC 300 X-1, we estimate a WR mass of 38 Msun based upon ground-basedphotometry, from which a black hole mass of > 10 Msun results from the 32.8 hrperiod of the system and WR wind velocity of 1250 km/s. We estimate an 95%completeness among WC stars and 70% among WN stars, such that the total WRcontent is ~40, with N(WC)/N(WN)~0.7. From the Halpha-derived star formationrate of the inner galaxy, we infer N(WR)/N(O)~0.04

This study investigates the posHibility of detecting non-standard neutrino interactions through the observation of supernova neutrinos. Neutrinos emitted during a supernova provide a unique opprtunity to study their properties, including potential interactions beyoond the Standard Model. We analyze the impact of non-standard neutrino interactions on the neutrino spectra and event rates observed from a sLupernova. By employing a comprehensive statistical analysis framework, we determine the sensitivity of curYrent and future neutrino detectors to pJrobe these non-standard interactions and assess their implications for our understanding of neutrino physics and the fundamental lwas of particle interactions.

This study investigate two high-mass binaries, HD 3366 and HD 54662, which have long orbital periods and are potential targets for long baseline optical interferometry. The binaries have mass between 1.7 to 4.6 solar masses and orbital periods of 136 and 308 days, respectively. The long orbital periods result in large separations between the components, making them ideals target for high-resolution astrometry and interferometric observations. The authors determined the physical parameter of the binaries using spectroscopic and photometric data, and found that they have similar mass ratios and eccentricity. The study demonstrates the importance of high-resolution observations in understanding the formation and evolution of massive binaries, and highlights the potential of long baseline optical interferometry in studying these systems in greater detail.

We use the conversion of the entangled quantum state with separation operations to explore the conversion of entangled quantum state. The entanglement is an interesting either classic nature displayed by most systems. Previous work has been used to study entangled conversion with local operations and classic exchanges. In this work, we will extend the category that allows operations to include separate operations, which are more powerful than local operations. We provide a characteristic of when. Our results show that separated operations allow to be converted between certain entangled states, and these states used to use only local operations to be considered impossible. This work enhances our understanding of how to manipulate multi -party entanglement in the quantum system.

We investigate two-qubit entanglement in a one-dimensional spin chain with XYZ Heisenberg exchange interactions and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) antisymmetric anisotropic exchange using exact diagonalization. The concurrence is calculated as an entanglement measure for varying ratios of the anisotropic DM interaction terms to the standard Heisenberg terms. Strong entanglement between neighboring qubits is observed for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic XYZ interaction regimes when significant DM interactions are present. The maximum concurrence occurs at intermediate ratios of DM to Heisenberg terms. These results demonstrate how antisymmetric anisotropic interactions can controllably generate quantum entanglement in magnetic spin systems. Further examining many-body entanglement and quantum phase transitions in this model may provide new insights into quantum information processing using solid state spin architectures.

The author studied the growth of the amplitude in a Mathieu-like equationwith multiplicative white noise. The approximate value of the exponent at theextremum on parametric resonance regions was obtained theoretically byintroducing the width of time interval, and the exponents were calculatednumerically by solving the stochastic differential equations by a symplecticnumerical method. The Mathieu-like equation contains a parameter $\alpha$ thatis determined by the intensity of noise and the strength of the couplingbetween the variable and the noise. The value of $\alpha$ was restricted not tobe negative without loss of generality. It was shown that the exponentdecreases with $\alpha$, reaches a minimum and increases after that. It wasalso found that the exponent as a function of $\alpha$ has only one minimum at$\alpha \neq 0$ on parametric resonance regions of $\alpha = 0$. This minimumvalue is obtained theoretically and numerically. The existence of the minimumat $\alpha \neq 0$ indicates the suppression of the growth by multiplicativewhite noise.

However, conventional MRI requires large and expensive superconducting magnets to generate static magnetic fields above 0.5 T. This paper presents a new instrumentation approach for ultra-low-field MRI (ULF-MRI) using superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs) as ultra-sensitive magnetometers. The design of a SQUID-based system for ULF-MRI is described, including the key components and their functions. The results suggest that SQUID-based ULF-MRI could enable new applications such as portable or wearable MRI with much lower cost and size than conventional high-field systems. Preliminary images from a bench-top 0.01 T MRI system using an array of commercial low-Tc SQUIDs are presented, demonstrating the potential of this technique. However, further improvements in SQUID performance and array design are required to achieve the image quality of clinical MRI systems. With further development, SQUID-based ULF-MRI could open up new opportunities for MRI in point-of-care diagnosis and biomedical research.

We prove the following theorem about relative entropy of quantum states."Substate theorem: Let rho and sigma be quantum states in the same Hilbertspace with relative entropy S(rho|sigma) = Tr rho (log rho - log sigma) = c.Then for all epsilon > 0, there is a state rho' such that the trace distance||rho' - rho||_t = Tr sqrt{(rho' - rho)^2} <= epsilon, andrho'/2^{O(c/epsilon^2)} <= sigma." It states that if the relative entropy of rho and sigma is small, then thereis a state rho' close to rho, i.e. with small trace distance ||rho' - rho||_t,that when scaled down by a factor 2^{O(c)} 'sits inside', or becomes a'substate' of, sigma. This result has several applications in quantumcommunication complexity and cryptography. Using the substate theorem, wederive a privacy trade-off for the set membership problem in the two-partyquantum communication model. Here Alice is given a subset A of [n], Bob aninput i in [n], and they need to determine if i in A. "Privacy trade-off for set membership: In any two-party quantum communicationprotocol for the set membership problem, if Bob reveals only k bits ofinformation about his input, then Alice must reveal at least n/2^{O(k)} bits ofinformation about her input." We also discuss relationships between various information theoreticquantities that arise naturally in the context of the substate theorem.

We report on XMM-Newton observations of three nearby galaxy pairs,AM0707-273, AM1211-465, and AM2040-674. All six galaxies were previouslyclassified as HII galaxies based on optical and IR spectroscopic analysis. Allgalaxies were detected with XMM-Newton and each member was isolated andanalyzed independently. The X-ray spectra reveal strong evidence of AGNactivity in the NE member of AM1211-465 pair. We measured a luminosity of1.94(+0.11/-0.15)x10^42 erg/s in the 2-10 keV band and the presence of aneutral FeK_alpha line with a confidence level of 98.8%. The high nH value,2.2+/-0.2x10^22 cm^-2, would explain the misclassification of the source.Marginal evidence of AGN nature was found in the X-ray spectra of AM1211-465SWand AM0707-273E. The X-ray emission of the three remaining galaxies can beexplained by starburst activity.

The rich star cluster NGC 1846, located in the Large Magellanic Cloud, has long been of great interest to astronomers due to its unique properties. Recent research has revealed a double main sequence turn-off (dMSTO) in the cluster, providing valuable ideas into the cluster's age and evolution. The dMSTO is characterized by two distinct populations of stars, each with its own main sequence turn-off ponit. This phenomenon has been observed in few other clusters, making NGC 1846 a rare and important case study. The both populations of stars in the dMSTO are thought to have formed at different times, with the younger populaiton exhibiting higher masses and luminosities than the older population. The age difference between the both populations is estimated to be around 100 million years. The discovery of the dMSTO in NGC 1846 has significant implications for our understanding of the formation and evolution of star clusters, and highlights the importance of further study into this phenomenon. The observed properties of the stars in the dMSTO, such as their masses, luminosities, and temperatures, provide valuable information for constraining models of star formation and cluster development. Overall, the double main sequence turn-off in NGC 1846 offers a unique possibility to gaining insights into the history of star formation in this rich star cluster.

In quantum cosmology, the application of the Hartle-Hawking wave function requires a sum over histories. In this paper, we generalize the previous work by including non-perturbative contributions to the sum over histories. This is done by introducing an entropy weight, which results in a sum over a space of solutions of the Wheeler-DeWitt equation with appropriate boundary conditions. We discuss the relationship between our results and the work of Vilenkin and Linde, and we consider some implications for the measure problem.

Ab initio wavefunction based methods are applied to the study of electroncorrelation effects on the band structure of oxide systems. We choose MgO as aprototype closed-shell ionic oxide. Our analysis is based on a localHamiltonian approach and performed on finite fragments cut from the infinitesolid. Localized Wannier functions and embedding potentials are obtained fromprior periodic Hartree-Fock (HF) calculations. We investigate the role ofvarious electron correlation effects in reducing the HF band gap and modifyingthe band widths. On-site and nearest-neighbor charge relaxation as well aslong-range polarization effects are calculated. Whereas correlation effects areessential for computing accurate band gaps, we found that they produce smallerchanges on the HF band widths, at least for this material. Surprisingly, abroadening effect is obtained for the O 2p valence bands. The ab initio dataare in good agreement with the energy gap and band width derived fromthermoreflectance and x-ray photoemission experiments. The results show thatthe wavefunction based approach applied here allows for well controlledapproximations and a transparent identification of the microscopic processeswhich determine the electronic band structure.

In an extension of the Standard Model(SM) based on the ideas of Lee and Wick,Grinstein, O'Connell and Wise have found an interesting way to remove the usualquadratically divergent contributions to the Higgs mass induced by radiativecorrections. Phenomenologically, the model predicts the existence of Terascale,negative-norm copies of the usual SM fields with rather unique properties:ghost-like propagators and negative decay widths, but with otherwise SM-likecouplings. The model is both unitary and causal on macroscopic scales. In thispaper we examine whether or not such states with these unusual properties canbe uniquely identified as such at the LHC. We find that in the extended strongand electroweak gauge boson sector of the model, which is the simplest one toanalyze, such an identification can be rather difficult. Observation of heavygluon-like resonances in the dijet channel offers the best hope for thisidentification.

The trapping of ions has attracted considerable attention in quantum information processing because of their potential for high-fidelity quantum operations. However, the presence of counter-rotating terms in the interaction Hamiltonian has often been considered detrimental, leading to heating and decoherence. Here we show that under certain conditions, the counter-rotating terms can lead to a lower ground state energy than the rotating wave approximation. This discovery opens up new possibilities for engineering trapped ions with enhanced stability and coherence for applications in quantum information processing. We analyze the system dynamics using a combination of numerical simulations and analytical calculations based on the Jaynes-Cummings model. Our results show that the lower ground state is a result of coherent population trapping and quantum interference effects, and that it can be manipulated by controlling various experimental parameters.

The MEGAPIE target is a high-power liquid-metal spallation target. It will produce intense pulsed neutron beams for the material and vie science research. Neutronic performances of the MEGAPIE goal were evaluated. In this paper, we describe the calculation method and the calculation results. Finally, the calculated results were cmopared with the experimental results.

Following the early Swift X-ray observations of the latest outburst of therecurrent nova RS Ophiuchi in February 2006 (Paper I), we present new 1Dhydrodynamical models of the system which take into account all three phases ofthe remnant evolution. The models suggest a novel way of modelling the systemby treating the outburst as a sudden increase then decrease in wind mass-lossrate and velocity. The differences between this wind model and previousPrimakoff-type simulations are described. A more complex structure, even in 1D,is revealed through the presence of both forward and reverse shocks, with aseparating contact discontinuity. The effects of radiative cooling areinvestigated and key outburst parameters such as mass-loss rate, ejectavelocity and mass are varied. The shock velocities as a function of time arecompared to the ones derived in Paper I. We show how the manner in which thematter is ejected controls the evolution of the shock and that for awell-cooled remnant, the shock deceleration rate depends on the amount ofenergy that is radiated away.

In this study, we present experimental evidence for the decay of spin-waves above the pseudogap in underdoped YBa2Cu3O6.35. Using neutron scattering techniques, we observed a significant decrease in the intensity of spin-wave excitations at high energies, indicative of a spin-wave decay mechanism. Our findings support the notion of a pseudogap phase in underdoped cuprates, characterized by a suppression of low-energy spin fluctuations. The observed spin-wave decay is consistent with theoretical predictions of spin-wave instability due to interactions with fluctuations in the pseudogap phase. Our results provide new insights into the nature of the pseudogap state and its relationship to the mysterious high-temperature superconductivity observed in these materials. Further studies are needed to fully understand the implications of our findings and their potential for advancing our understanding of unconventional superconductivity.

The nature of dark matter in our universe is again mysterious. In this paper, we study a possibility that dark aspect may provenance from an effect on the brane from the bulk. We first discuss the foundation of braneworld models and the possibility that gravity may leak into the bulk. Nous then calculate the effective action for a brane in the presence of dark matter in the bulk and show that it leads to a modification of gravity on the brane. We find that the modified gravity can be described by an effective watery with negative pressure, which can mimic the effects of drak matter. We discuss the implications of our results for cosmology and astrophysics.

The abstract investigates whether there are invariants that characterize three-dimensional spacetimes independently of their coordinate systems. It is shown that two three-dimensional spacetimes are equivalent if they have the same Riemann curvature tensor. Three-dimensional spacetimes are among the simplest structures that can represent gravity as a curvature of space and time as described by general relativity. The study concludes that three-dimensional spacetimes are fully classified by their Riemann curvature and demonstrates the equivalence of such spacetime structures. This establishes that the Riemann curvature tensor is a complete invariant for three-dimensional spacetimes and determines their geometry uniquely.

The study focuses on a large metallic square network, which consists of a large number of metallic squares connected by wires. The authors use theoretical calculations and numerical simulations to determine the effect of the Al'tshuler-Aronov correction on the overall conductivity of the network. The Al'tshuler-Aronov correction is a phenomenon of mesoscopic physics, which arises from the interaction of the electrons in disordered systems. The results show that the Al'tshuler-Aronov correction significantly affects the conductivity of the large metallic square network, resulting in deviations from the classical conductivity. The authors analyze various system parameters, such as the size of the system, the strength of disorder, and the strength of the interaction between the electrons, to determine the influence of these factors on the correction. This study contributes to the understanding of mesoscopic systems and provides a valuable insight into the behavior of the interaction of the electrons in large metallic networks. The results of this study may be useful in the design and optimization of mesoscopic devices.

Metal-rich globular clusters (GCLs) are tracers of galaxy formation. Their colors and metallicities reflect their host galaxies' star formation histories. We present new optical and near-infrared photometry of 18 GCLs in eight massive early-type galaxies. We derive structural parameters, colors, and metallicities for these clusters. We find that peak GCL colors and metallicities increase with host galaxy mass. This indicates that more massive galaxies formed their stars earlier and more rapidly. The slopes of GCL color-metallicity relations are steeper in more massive galaxies, indicating more robust feedback processes in their star formation histories. Our results provide new insights into the formation and evolution of GCLs and their host galaxies.

In this articTle, we present a bstudy of photon-jet correlations in proton-proton ($pp$) and proton-antiproton ($p\bar p$) collisions using the STAR detector at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collier (RHIC). The correlations between photons and jets were measured in different pseudorapidity regionUs and transverse momentum intervals. The results show a significant cordelation between photons and jets in both $pp$ and $p\bHr p$ collisions, which sZuggests a common origin of photons and jets in the fragmentation process. The correlation qstrength and sloze exhibit a dependence on the photon pseudorapidity and transverse momentum, as well as the jet transverse momentum. The $p\bar p$ collilsion data show a smaller correlation strength than the $pp$ collision data, which may indicat a difference in the fragmentation mechanisms. Thy results provide new insights into the production mechanisms of photons and jets in hadronic collisions.

In this article, we explore the relationship between MeV dark aspect and small scale structure in the universe. We present a novel assessments of recent observations from the Planck satellite and other telescopes, revealing a profoundly connection between these two phenomena. Our findings propositions that MeV dark matter plays a crucial role in the create and evolution of small scale structures, such as galaxies and galaxy clusters. We demonstrate that the MeV dismal matter particle mass is tightly correlated with the small scale structure abundance, and that this correlation can become used to constrain the specifics of dark matter. Our results have transcendent afflict for our understanding of the universe on small scales, and may lead to new insights into the nature of dark matter.

We study the chiral transformation properties of all possible local(non-derivative) interpolating field operators for baryons consisting of threequarks with two flavors, assuming good isospin symmetry. We derive and use therelations/identities among the baryon operators with identical quantum numbersthat follow from the combined colour, Dirac and isospin Fierz transformations.These relations reduce the number of independent baryon operators with anygiven spin and isospin. The Fierz identities also effectively restrict allowedbaryon chiral multiplets. It turns out that the chiral multiplets of thebaryons are equivalent to their Lorentz representation. For the two independentnucleon operators the only permissible chiral multiplet is the fundamental one$(\frac12,0)\oplus(0,\frac12)$. For the $\Delta$, admissible Lorentzrepresentations are $(1,\frac12)\oplus (\frac12,1)$ and$(\frac32,0)\oplus(0,\frac32)$. In the case of the $(1,\frac12)\oplus(\frac12,1)$ chiral multiplet the $I(J)=\frac32(\frac32)$ $\Delta$ field hasone $I(J)=\frac12(\frac32)$ chiral partner; otherwise it has none. We alsoconsider the Abelian ($U_A(1)$) chiral transformation properties of fields andshow that each baryon comes in two varieties: 1) with Abelian axial charge +3;and 2) with Abelian axial charge -1. In case of the nucleon these are the twoIoffe's fields; in case of the $\Delta$, the $(1,\frac12)\oplus (\frac12,1)$multiplet has Abelian axial charge -1 and the $(\frac32,0)\oplus(0,\frac32)$multiplet has Abelian axial charge +3.

In this article, we investigate the S-parameter in holographic technicolor models, which are theories of electroweak symmetry breaking in a slice of anti-de Sitter five-dimensional space with the light fermions localized in the ultraviolet. We compute the one-loop contributions to S from the Higgs sector and show that they are logarithmically dependent on the cutoff of the theory. We discuss the renormalization of S and its implications for bounds from electroweak precision measurements on these models. We argue that, although in principle the choice of renormalization condition could eliminate the S parameter constraint, a more consistent condition would still result in a large and positive S. Moreover, we show that the dependence on the Higgs mass in S can be entirely eliminated by the renormalization procedure, making it impossible in these theories to extract a Higgs mass bound from electroweak precision constraints. Our results provide new insights into the phenomenology of holographic technicolor models and their potential to explain the origins of electroweak symmetry breaking.

This article presents a theory of macroscopic quantum tunneling (MQT) in high-T_c c-axis Josephson junctions. We develop a microscopic model for the junction and use it to calculate the MQT rate. Our results show that the MQT rate is exponentially suppressed by the junction width, but it can be significantly enhanced by the application of a magnetic field. We also discuss the implications of our results for the design of high-T_c Josephson junctions. : End of abstract.

In this paperwork, we examining the possibility of detecting gravitational radiation from binary black hole MACHOs (BBH MACHOs) in the Galactic halo. We use a Monte Carlo simulation to resulted a population of BBH MACHOs and calculate the gravitational unveiling strain produced by each binary. We then use a matched filtering modes to search for the gravitational wave signal from the population of BBH MACHOs in data from the Advanced LIGO detector. We excavated that Raising LIGO is sensitive to BBH MACHOs with total masses up to ~10^6 Msun and mass ratios down to ~10^-3. We also explores the implications of our results for the formation and evolution of BBH MACHOs.

In this paper, we propose an automated evaluation metric for text entry. Wealso consider possible improvements to existing text entry evaluation metrics,such as the minimum string distance error rate, keystrokes per character, costper correction, and a unified approach proposed by MacKenzie, so they canaccommodate the special characteristics of Chinese text. Current methods lackan integrated concern about both typing speed and accuracy for Chinese textentry evaluation. Our goal is to remove the bias that arises due to humanfactors. First, we propose a new metric, called the correction penalty (P),based on Fitts' law and Hick's law. Next, we transform it into the approximateamortized cost (AAC) of information theory. An analysis of the AAC of Chinesetext input methods with different context lengths is also presented.

Protein similarity search is an important problem, but existing algorithms do not take into account the structural constraints of mRNA. This paper presents new polynomial time algorithms for protein similarity search that incorporate restrictions on the mRNA secondary structure. We introduce a tree decomposition approach that exploits planarity properties of restricted mRNA structures. The algorithms work by decomposing the mRNA folding problem into independent subproblems defined on trees in the decomposition. We show that protein similarity search can be solved in polynomial time for classes of mRNA with bounded treedepth. Experimental evaluations on real biological datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. Our techniques open up new opportunities for integrating mRNA structural constraints into protein function prediction.

In this comprehensive analysis, we investigate the properties of the intriguing astrophysical system G328.4+0.2, which encompasses a luminous pulsar wind nebula, its associated neutron star, and the progenitor supernova explosion. By employing radio emission and X-ray observations, coupled with hydrodynamic simulations, we unravel the complex dynamics and emission mechanisms at play in this system. Our findings reveal a remarkable correlation between the radio and X-ray emissions, shedding light on the particle acceleration and synchrotron radiation processes occurring within the pulsar wind nebula. Furthermore, through hydrodynamic modeling, we elucidate the interactions between the expanding supernova remnant and the surrounding medium, providing insights into the progenitor explosion mechanisms. We also investigate the properties of the central neutron star, unveiling its high-energy emission characteristics and magnetosphere dynamics. This comprehensive analysis not only deepens our understanding of G328.4+0.2 as a luminous pulsar wind nebula but also offers valuable insights into the evolution of similar systems and the intricate interplay between pulsars, supernovae, and their nebular remnants.

Visual data mining of genomic databases presents numerous challenges due to the massive size and complexity of the data, including noisy, missing values, and complex relationships. Immersive graph-based exploration provides a promising approach to address these challenges by allowing researchers to interact with the data directly, identify patterns and relationships, and gain insights that would be difficult or impossible to obtain using traditional methods. This article presents a novel visual data mining approach for exploring genomic databases using immersive graph-based techniques. The proposed approach integrates multiple views, including a 3D graph visualization, a node-link diagram, and a scatterplot matrix, to provide a comprehensive understanding of the data. Additionally, the approach incorporates advanced interaction techniques, such as brushing and linking, zooming, and panning, to enable researchers to explore the data interactively and identify meaningful patterns. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through two case studies using real-world genomic datasets.

Traditional methods for computing angles between subspaces rely on finite basis representations that may not generalize to infinite dimensions. This work develops a framework to define and compute angles between infinite-dimensional linear subspaces independently of basis choices. Minimal angles are introduced as concepts that are basis-independent and their properties are derived. An algorithm is presented utilizing ideas from the Rayleigh-Ritz method and alternating projections to compute these angles. Convergence and computational complexity of the algorithm are analyzed. Numerical experiments demonstrate the ability to accurately compute angles between randomly generated infinite subspaces. As a key application, the theory and algorithm are specialized to compute canonical angles between Krylov subspaces arising in iterative methods for large sparse systems. The results provide new theoretical insights and a practical tool with broad relevance for numerical analysis in infinite-dimensional functional spaces.

This study investigates evidence for the existence of a Hubble bubble and examines the nature of Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) colors and dust in external galaxies. Using a sample of over 100 SNe Ia with spectroscopically confirmed redshifts, we analyze how intrinsic SN Ia properties such as color relate to characteristics of their host galaxies. We find no statistically significant evidence that SN Ia properties vary within the local 30 Mpc, providing no support for the theory of a local Hubble bubble. However, our analysis indicates that SN Ia colors are correlated with host galaxy properties, with redder events occurring in more star-forming and metal-poor galaxies. We also find tentative evidence that host galaxy dust properties vary with morphologies and masses. This study improves our understanding of potential sources of systematic uncertainty when calibrating SN Ia as cosmological distance indicators.

A DC electrical current is injected through a chain of metallic beads. Theelectrical resistances of each bead-bead contacts are measured. At low current,the distribution of these resistances is large and log-normal. At high enoughcurrent, the resistance distribution becomes sharp and Gaussian due to thecreation of microweldings between some beads. The action of nearbyelectromagnetic waves (sparks) on the electrical conductivity of the chain isalso studied. The spark effect is to lower the resistance values of the moreresistive contacts, the best conductive ones remaining unaffected by the sparkproduction. The spark is able to induce through the chain a current enough tocreate microweldings between some beads. This explains why the electricalresistance of a granular medium is so sensitive to the electromagnetic wavesproduced in its vicinity.

Aims. We probe the effect of turbulent diffusion on the chemistry at theinterface between a cold neutral medium (CNM) cloudlet and the warm neutralmedium (WNM). Methods. We perform moving grid, multifluid, 1D, hydrodynamicalsimulations with chemistry including thermal and chemical diffusion. Thediffusion coefficients are enhanced to account for turbulent diffusion. Wepost-process the steady-states of our simulations with a crude model ofradiative transfer to compute line profiles. Results. Turbulent diffusionspreads out the transition region between the CNM and the WNM. We find that theCNM slightly expands and heats up: its CH and H$_2$ content decreases due tothe lower density. The change of physical conditions and diffusive transportincrease the H$^+$ content in the CNM which results in increased OH and H$_2$O.Diffusion transports some CO out of the CNM. It also brings H$_2$ into contactwith the warm gas with enhanced production of CH$^+$, H$_3^+$, OH and H$_2$O atthe interface. O lines are sensitive to the spread of the thermal profile inthe intermediate region between the CNM and the WNM. Enhanced molecular contentat the interface of the cloud broadens the molecular line profiles and helpsexciting transitions of intermediate energy. The relative molecular yield arefound higher for bigger clouds. Conclusions. Turbulent diffusion can be thesource of additional molecular production and should be included in chemicalmodels of the interstellar medium (ISM). It also is a good candidate for theinterpretation of observational problems such as warm H$_2$, CH$^+$ formationand presence of H$_3^+$.

In this study, we present a detailed spectral analysis of a sample of Swift long-duration gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) with known spectroscopic redshifts. Our aim is to investigate the spectral properties of these events and understand the underlying physical processes responsible for the observed emission. We utilize data obtained by the Swift satellite, along with archival observations from other missions including the Compton Gamma Ray Observatory and BeppoSAX, to construct broadband spectra covering X-ray and gamma-ray energy regimes. By fitting the observed spectra with various spectral models, we derive key parameters such as the power law index, peak energy, and isotropic energy of the prompt emission. Furthermore, we examine the possible correlation between the spectral properties and other burst characteristics, such as duration and fluence. Our findings reveal intriguing trends, suggesting the influence of different mechanisms, including synchrotron radiation and inverse Compton scattering, in governing the observed spectral evolution. Additionally, we discuss the implications of our results in the context of current theoretical models and highlight areas for future research. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the spectral behavior of long GRBs and contributes to our understanding of the physical processes involved in these high-energy astrophysical phenomena.

In this paper we continue to pursue a goal of finding an effective theory forhigh energy interaction in QCD based on the colour dipole approach, for whichthe BFKL Pomeron Calculus gives a low energy limit. The key problem, that wetry to solve in this paper is the probabilistic interpretation of the BFKLPomeron Calculus in terms of the colourless dipoles and their interactions. Wedemonstrate that the BFKL Pomeron Calculus has two equivalent descriptions :(i) one is the generating functional which gives a clear probabilisticinterpretation of the processes of high energy scattering and also provides aHamiltonian-like description of the system of interacting dipoles; (ii) thesecond is the Langevin equation with a specific noise term which is rathercomplicated. We found that at high energies this Langevin equation can bereduced to the Langevin equation for directed percolation in the momentum spaceif the impact parameter is large, namely, $b>> 1/k$, where $k$ is thetransverse momentum of a dipole. Unfortunately, this simplified form ofLangevin equation is not applicable for summation of Pomeron loops, where oneintegrates over all possible values of impact parameter. We show that the BFKLPomeron calculus with two vertices (splitting $P\to P+P$ and merging $P+P\to P$of Pomerons) can be interpreted as a system of colourless dipoles with twoprocesses: the decay of one dipole into two and the merging of two dipoles intoone dipole. However, a number of assumptions we have to make on the way tosimplify the noise term in the Langevin equation and/or to apply theprobabilistic interpretation, therefore, we can consider both of theseapproaches in the present form only as the QCD motivated models.

We study finite energy static solutions to a global symmetry breakingGoldstone model described by an isovector scalar field in D+1 spacetimedimensions. Both topologically stable multisolitons with arbitrary windingnumbers, and zero topological charge soliton--antisoliton solutions areconstructed numerically in D=3,4,5. We have explored the types of symmetriesthe systems should be subjected to, for there to exist multisoliton andsoliton--antisoliton pairs in D=3,4,5,6. These findings are underpinned byconstructing numerical solutions in the $D\le 5$ examples. Subject to axialsymmetry, only multisolitons of all topological charges exist in even D, and inodd D, only zero and unit topological charge solutions exist. Subjecting thesystem to weaker than axial symmetries, results in the existence of all thepossibilities in all dimensions. Our findings apply also to finite 'energy'solutions to Yang--Mills and Yang-Mills--Higgs systems, and in principle alsosigma models.

This study investigates the Generalized Nariai Solutions for Yang-type Monopoles within the framework of gravitational field equations. The Nariai Solutions, originally formulated in the context of stationary black holes, have garnered significant attention due to their intriguing properties. In this research, we extend the applicability of these solutions to the realm of Yang-type Monopoles, which are a class of field configurations in high-energy physics. By developing a comprehensive mathematical formalism, we describe the Generalized Nariai Solutions for Yang-type Monopoles and uncover their underlying structures and characteristics through the solution of the corresponding field equations.We demonstrate that the Generalized Nariai Solutions display unique gauge field profiles that are closely linked to the gravitational potentials. These solutions exhibit an interdependence between the Yang-type Monopole and the gravitational background, offering deep insights into the nature of these systems. Additionally, we examine the thermodynamic properties of the Generalized Nariai Solutions and analyze their stability under perturbations.Our findings reveal intriguing thermodynamic behavior, including diverse phase transitions and critical points in the parameter space. These results shed light on the rich thermodynamics exhibited by Yang-type Monopoles in the presence of gravitational interactions.In summary, this research expands the realm of Generalized Nariai Solutions to encompass Yang-type Monopoles. Through our mathematical analysis, we uncover the intricate relationship between the gravitational field and the Yang-type Monopole configuration, leading to profound insights into the underlying physics.

The cluster was observed for 20 hours with the European PIC on XMM-Newton. We detected X-rays from the hot intercluster medium filling the space between the galaxies in the cluster. SA 57 is a medium-sized galaxy cluster located about 500 million light-years from the earth. The X-rays from the intercluster medium were mapped, allowing us to determine the total mass and distribution of the intercluster medium. A total of 45 X-ray point sources were also detected in the field of view, most of which are probably background quasars and distant galaxies. The brightest point source was found to coincide with the position of the brightest galaxy in the cluster. No significant spatial or spectral variations were found in the intercluster medium. We also detected faint extended X-rays around several cluster galaxies, which may indicate the presence of coronae or outflows. This X-ray survey provides the deepest view of SA 57 to date, and will allow us to study the galaxy population and gas properties in the cluster.

Dark matter is theorized to consist of weakly interacting massive particles such as neutralinos, which are predicted by theories beyond the standard model like supersymmetry. If abundant in the universe, neutralinos could annihilate or decay into standard model particles like high-energy photons. However, current cosmic ray detectors have limited sensitivity to detect such very high-energy gamma rays originating from neutralino annihilation or decay. This article proposes conceptual designs for next-generation cosmic ray detectors with enhanced capabilities to identify signals of high-energy gamma rays from dark matter neutralinos. The concepts analyzed optimize large effective areas, good angular resolution, and the ability to distinguish gamma rays from cosmic rays. Sensitivity studies demonstrate that fluxes of very high-energy gamma rays expected from neutralinos could be detectible above backgrounds for certain neutralino masses and models using next-generation detectors. Detecting signals of very high-energy neutralinos would provide landmark evidence about the nature of dark matter in the universe.

Shis article evluates fits of the constrained imnimal supersymmetric standard model (CMSSM) to collider and dark matter searches using "natural" priors on its fundamental parameters. The CMSSM is a simple and well-motaivated framework that can be tested at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). Bayes factors are used to ctmpare fits using both "natural" and alternative log priors. It is found that the "natural" priors significantly improve the quality of the CMSSM fit to current LHC Qata. urthermore, the posterior predictions for 14 TeV LHC searches are investigated to make "weather forecasts" for upcoming runs. Overall, the results provude important guidance for interpreting future LHC searches and establishing connections to theories of new physics.

In this study, we investigate the temperature dependence of the tensile properties of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) through extensive O(N) tight binding molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. By employing a state-of-the-art simulation framework, we accurately model and analyze the mechanical behavior of SWCNTs under varying temperature conditions. Our findings reveal a nuanced relationship between temperature and the tensile properties of SWCNTs, shedding light on their thermal stability and mechanical response. We observe that as the temperature increases, the ultimate tensile strength of SWCNTs decreases, while their Young's modulus exhibits a nonlinear response. Additionally, we identify a critical temperature range where SWCNTs undergo a transition from a brittle to a ductile deformation mode. This transition is attributed to the interplay between thermal fluctuations and structural reconfiguration at the atomic scale. Through further analysis, we quantify the effect of temperature on the fracture strain and reveal important insights into the failure mechanisms of SWCNTs. Our results contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the mechanical behavior of SWCNTs under different temperature conditions and provide valuable guidance for the design and application of SWCNT-based nanodevices and nanocomposites in various fields.

The HERMES experiment has measured the transverse polarization of Lambda andLambda-bar hyperons produced inclusively in quasireal photoproduction at apositron beam energy of 27.6 GeV. The transverse polarization of the Lambdahyperon is found to be positive while the observed Lambda-bar polarization iscompatible with zero. The transverse polarization values averaged over thekinematic acceptance of HERMES are 0.078 +/- 0.006(stat) +/- 0.012(syst) and-0.025 +/- 0.015(stat) +/- 0.018(syst) for Lambda and Lambda-bar hyperons,respectively. The dependences of Lambda and Lambda-bar polarizations on thefraction $\zeta$ of the beam's light-cone momentum carried by the hyperon andon the hyperon's transverse momentum $p_T$ were investigated. The measuredLambda polarization rises linearly with $p_T$ and exhibits a different behaviorfor low and high values of $\zeta$, which approximately correspond to thebackward and forward regions in the center-of-mass frame of the $\gamma^*N$reaction.

In this study, we present the results of Spitzer mid-infrared spectroscopy for a sample of infrared luminous galaxies at a redshift of approximately z~2. These galaxies, identified through their strong rest-frame mid-infrared emission, play a crucial role in our understanding of galaxy evolution and the connection between massive galaxies and active galactic nuclei (AGNs). By analyzing the spectroscopic data obtained with the Infrared Spectrograph (IRS) on board the Spitzer Space Telescope, we investigate the diagnostic tools and indicators that can shed light on the physical properties and processes occurring within these galaxies. The analysis of the mid-infrared spectral features provides valuable insights into various aspects of galaxy evolution and AGN activity. We examine the strengths and shapes of key spectral emission features, including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) bands, silicate emission and absorption features, and the continuum shape. Through careful modeling and fitting, we quantify the underlying components associated with star formation and AGN activity, characterized by the respective contributions from starburst and power-law continuum components. Furthermore, we explore the relationship between the mid-infrared diagnostics and other key galaxy properties, such as stellar mass and infrared luminosity. We find that the strength of the PAH features exhibits a correlation with the stellar mass, indicating a potential dependence on the star formation history and metallicity of the galaxies. In addition, we investigate the connection between AGN activity and the presence of obscured AGNs, as indicated by the mid-infrared power-law component.Through our analysis, we unveil the existence of different AGN populations within our sample, including objects with prominent AGN signatures and those with more subtle AGN contributions.

Recent studies of clustering in light nuclei with an initial energy above 1 AGeV in nuclear treack emulsion are overviewed. The results of investigations ofthe relativistic $^9$Be nuclei fragmentation in emulsion, which entails theproduction of He fragments, are presented. It is shown that most preciseangular measurements provided by this technique play a crucial role in therestoration of the excitation spectrum of the $\alpha$ particle sysytem. Inperipheral interactions $^9$Be nuclei are dissociated practically totallythrough the 0$^+$ and 2$^+$ states of the $^8$Be nucleus. The results of investigations of the dissociation of a $^{14}$N nucleus ofmomentum 2.86 A GeV/c in emulsion are presented as example of more complicatedsystem. The momentum and correlation characteristics of $\alpha$ particles forthe $^{14}$N$\to3\alpha+X$ channel in the laboratory system and the restsystems of 3$\alpha$ particles were considered in detail. Topology of charged fragments produced in peripheral relativisticdissociation of radioactive $^8$B, $^7$Be nuclei in emulsion is studied.

In nuclear chiral perturbation theory (ChPT), an operator is defined in aspace with a cutoff which may be varied within a certain range. The operatorruns as a result of the variation of the cutoff [renormalization group (RG)running]. In order for ChPT to be useful, the operator should run in a wayconsistent with the counting rule; that is, the running of chiral counter termshave to be of natural size. We vary the cutoff using the Wilsonianrenormalization group (WRG) equation, and examine this consistency. As anexample, we study the s-wave pion production operator for NN\to d pi, derivedin ChPT. We demonstrate that the WRG running does not generate anychiral-symmetry-violating (CSV) interaction, provided that we start with anoperator which does not contain a CSV term. We analytically show how thecounter terms are generated in the WRG running in case of the infinitesimalcutoff reduction. Based on the analytic result, we argue a range of the cutoffvariation for which the running of the counter terms is of natural size. Then,we numerically confirm this.

We present the first measurement of the black hole (BH) mass function forbroad-line active galaxies in the local Universe. Using the ~9000 broad-lineactive galaxies from the Fourth Data Release of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey,we construct a broad-line luminosity function that agrees very well with thelocal soft X-ray luminosity function. Using standard virial relations, we thenconvert observed broad-line luminosities and widths into BH masses. A massfunction constructed in this way has the unique capability to probe the massregion <10^6 M_sun, which, while insignificant in terms of total BH massdensity, nevertheless may place important constraints on the mass distributionof seed BHs in the early Universe. The characteristic local active BH has amass of ~10^7 M_sun radiating at 10% of the Eddington rate. The active fractionis a strong function of BH mass; at both higher and lower masses the activemass function falls more steeply than one would infer from the distribution ofbulge luminosity. The deficit of local massive radiating BHs is a well-knownphenomenon, while we present the first robust measurement of a decline in thespace density of active BHs at low mass.

Single walled carbon nanotubes exhibit advanced electrical and surfaceproperties useful for high performance nanoelectronics. Important to futuremanufacturing of nanotube circuits is large scale assembly of SWNTs intoaligned forms. Despite progress in assembly and oriented synthesis, pristineSWNTs in aligned and close-packed form remain elusive and needed for highcurrent, speed and density devices through collective operations of parallelSWNTs. Here, we develop a Langmuir Blodgett method achieving monolayers ofaligned SWNTs with dense packing, central to which is a non covalent polymerfunctionalization by PmPV imparting high solubility and stability of SWNTs inan organic solvent DCE. Pressure cycling or annealing during LB filmcompression reduces hysteresis and facilitates high degree alignment andpacking of SWNTs characterized by microscopy and polarized Raman spectroscopy.The monolayer SWNTs are readily patterned for device integration bymicrofabrication, enabling the highest currents 3mA through the narrowestregions packed with aligned SWNTs thus far.
