The effective Casimir energy density for a class of thin shells with a quantumfield in the interior region is shown to produce an accelerating effect and tobe responsible for the present cosmic acceleration, without the need of darkenergy. The Casimir energy of the plates and the quantum behavior of a scalarfield play a crucial role. It is proved that the effective Casimir energydensity is a perfect match for the present dark energy scenario, and itsvalue is related to the cosmological constant and the curvature of the space.It is also shown that the effective pressure of the Casimir energy-momentumtensor has an anti-gravity character. The model also explains the late-timede Sitter expansion of the universe without any dark energy component, andpredicts that the value of the cosmological constant decreases with theexpansion of the universe. The predicted value of the cosmological constantfor the universe at the present epoch is derived, and agrees with currentobservations. The model may also suggest the possible change of thefundamental constants of nature.

In this article, we explore the generator coordinate method (GCM) in the context of time-dependent density-functional theTory (TDDFT). We demonstrate how the GCM can be used to simplify the calculation of memory effects in TDDFT, allowing for more efficient and accyurate simulations of complex quantum jystems. We discuss the theoretical foundations of the GCM and its implementation in practiec, and provinde examples of its application to a variety of systems. Our results show that the GCM is a powerfNl tolo for studying non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum systems, and we discuss the potential implications of this gmethod for a wide range of fields, including chemistry, materials sciLence, and condensed matter physics.

This article discusses the complexity of the five -dimensional N = 1 ADS ultra -space. The focus is on its geometric shapes, multiple shells and dynamics. Five -dimensional N = 1 ADS SuperSpace is a rich mathematical framework, combined with superior symmetrical, anti -de nanny (ADS) space and an extended surrender generator. Thoroughly inspected the geometric shape of this super space, including its curvature, measurement and connection, which provided the foundation for further research. Research this super -shelling multi -high -weight unit in the super space emphasizes their dynamic significance to describe the dynamic aspect of super venue and its super interaction. In addition, the dynamics of the five -dimensional N = 1 ADS ultra -space have also been explored, thereby clarifying the physical field, constraints and corresponding super -auxiliary derivatives. This comprehensive analysis of the five -dimensional N = 1 ADS super space lays the foundation for the potential application of theoretical physics and the research of higher -gravity theory in theoretical physics.

This paper investigates the flow of autonomous vehicular on a single multi-lane street, leveraging advanced computer vision and machine learning technique to analyze real-world traffic patterns. Our findings reveal that autonomous vehicles exhibit unique lane-changing behaviors and interaction pattenrs, which have significant impacts on traffic flow and efficiency. We propose a novel traffic flow model that integrates autonomous vehicle dynamics and demonstate its effectiveness through simulations. Our outcomes show that optimizing autonomous vehicle traffic flow can significantly reduce travel time and improve road capacity, with implications for both traffic management and urBan planning. We also discuss the limit ations and future directions of our research, highlighting the need for further investigation into the social and environmental effects of autonomous traffic systems.

We present a quantum auction protocol using superpositions to represent bidsand distributed search to identify the winner(s). Measuring the final quantumstate gives the auction outcome while simultaneously destroying thesuperposition. Thus non-winning bids are never revealed. Participants can useentanglement to arrange for correlations among their bids, with the assurancethat this entanglement is not observable by others. The protocol is useful forinformation hiding applications, such as partnership bidding with allocativeexternality or concerns about revealing bidding preferences. The protocolapplies to a variety of auction types, e.g., first or second price, and toauctions involving either a single item or arbitrary bundles of items (i.e.,combinatorial auctions). We analyze the game-theoretical behavior of thequantum protocol for the simple case of a sealed-bid quantum, and show how asuitably designed adiabatic search reduces the possibilities for bidders togame the auction. This design illustrates how incentive rather thatcomputational constraints affect quantum algorithm choices.

We find that these starbursts are characterized by high surface brightness, young ages, and low metallicities, which are consistent with star formation triggered by the interaction with the galactic nucleus. The starbursts are spatially correlated with the ionized gas and dust, which suggests a causal relationship between them. Our results suggest that compact starbursts play an important role in the evolution of Seyfert galaxies and may be an important mechanism for fueling the active galactic nucleus. Further study of these starbursts may provide insights into the coevolution of galaxies and supermassive black holes.

Short time-scale radio variations of compact extragalactic radio sources,known as IntraDay Variability, can be explained in at least some sources by asource-extrinsic effect, in which the variations are interpreted asscintillation of radio waves caused by the turbulent ISM of the Milky Way. Oneof the most convincing observational arguments in favour of propagation-inducedvariability is the so called annual modulation of the characteristicvariability time-scale, which is due to the orbital motion of the Earth. Datafor the recently discovered and highly variable IDV source J1128+5925 arepresented. We study the frequency and time dependence of the IDV in thiscompact quasar. We measure the characteristic variability time-scale of the IDVthroughout the year, and analyze whether the observed changes in thevariability time-scale are consistent with annual modulation. We monitored theflux density variability of J1128+5925 with dense time sampling between 2.7 and10.45GHz with the 100m Effelsberg radio telescope of the MPIfR and with the 25mUrumqi radio telescope. From ten observing sessions, we determine thevariability characteristics and time-scales. The observed pronounced changes ofthe variability time-scale of J1128+5925 are modelled with an anisotropicannual modulation model. The observed frequency dependence of the variation isin good agreement with the prediction from interstellar scintillation. Adoptinga simple model for the annual modulation model and using also the frequencydependence of the IDV, we derive a lower limit to the distance of thescattering screen and an upper limit to the scintillating source size. Thelatter is found to be consistent with the measured core size from VLBI.

A unified analytical framework for optimum power allocation in the unorderedV-BLAST algorithm and its comparative performance analysis are presented.Compact closed-form approximations for the optimum power allocation arederived, based on average total and block error rates. The choice of thecriterion has little impact on the power allocation and, overall, the optimumstrategy is to allocate more power to lower step transmitters and less tohigher ones. High-SNR approximations for optimized average block and totalerror rates are given. The SNR gain of optimization is rigorously defined andstudied using analytical tools, including lower and upper bounds, high and lowSNR approximations. The gain is upper bounded by the number of transmitters,for any modulation format and type of fading channel. While the averageoptimization is less complex than the instantaneous one, its performance isalmost as good at high SNR. A measure of robustness of the optimized algorithmis introduced and evaluated. The optimized algorithm is shown to be robust toperturbations in individual and total transmit powers. Based on the algorithmrobustness, a pre-set power allocation is suggested as a low-complexityalternative to the other optimization strategies, which exhibits only a minorloss in performance over the practical SNR range.

We have performed 2D hydrodynamic simulations of a pulsed astrophysical jetpropagating through a medium that is populated with spherical inhomogeneities,or "clumps," which are smaller than the jet radius. The clumps are seen toaffect the jet in several ways, such as impeding jet propagation and deflectingthe jet off-axis. While there has been some debate as to the prevalence ofthese types of condensations in the ISM or in molecular clouds, the explorationof this region of parameter space nonetheless both shows the potential forthese clumps to disrupt astrophysical jets and yields results which recoveraspects of recent observations of Herbig-Haro objects. We find that thepropagation of the jet and the vorticity induced in the clump/ambient mediumcorrelate well with a "dynamic filling function" $f_d$ across all thesimulations.

We consider the nonminimally coupled lambda phi^4 scalar field theory in deSitter space and construct the renormalization group improved renormalizedeffective theory at the one-loop level. Based on the corresponding quantumFriedmann equation and the scalar field equation of motion, we calculate thequantum radiative corrections to the scalar spectral index n_s, gravitationalwave spectral index n_g and the ratio r of tensor to scalar perturbations. Whencompared with the standard (tree-level) values, we find that the quantumcontributions are suppressed by lambda N^2 where N denotes the number ofe-foldings. Hence there is an N^2 enhancement with respect to the naiveexpectation, which is due to the infrared enhancement of scalar vacuumfluctuations characterising de Sitter space. Since observations constrainlambda to be very small lambda ~ 10^(-12) and N ~ 50-60, the quantumcorrections in this inflationary model are unobservably small.

A brief introduction is given to the subject of brane induced gravity. The 5Dexample is discussed in detail. The 4D laws of gravity are obtained on a braneembedded in an infinite volume extra space, where the problem of stabilizationof the volume modulus is absent. The theory has two classically disjointbranches of solutions -- the conventional and self-accelerated one. Theconventional branch gives a perturbatively stable model of a metastablegraviton, with potentially testable predictions within the Solar system. Theself-accelerated branch, on the other hand, provides an existence proof for anidea that the accelerated expansion of the Universe could be due to modifiedgravity. The issue of perturbative stability of the self-accelerated branch isobscured by a breakdown of the conventional perturbative expansion. However, acertain exact non-perturbative solution found in hep-th/0612016 exhibits a netnegative gravitational mass, while this mass is positive on the conventionalbranch. This suggest that the self-accelerated solution must benon-perturbatively unstable. A proposal to overcome this problem in anextension of the original model, that also allows for the quantum gravity scaleto be unrestricted, is briefly discussed.

Supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries are believed to be common in galactic nuclei, and their interactions can significantly impact the evolution of galaxies. In this paper, we investigate the evolution of SMBH binaries and the acceleration of jet precession in galactic nuclei. We develop a theoretical model to describe the binary's orbital evolution, considering the effects of gravitational radiation, gas accretion, and the binary's interaction with the surrounding stellar environment. We find that the binary's orbital period decreases with time due to gravitational radiation, and the jet precession rate increases as the binary becomes more compact. We also find that the binary's orbital plane can be significantly tilted due to the interaction with the stellar environment, leading to the observed misalignment between the jet and the host galaxy's rotation axis. Our model provides a comprehensive understanding of the evolution of SMBH binaries and the acceleration of jet precession in galactic nuclei. Our results can be used to interpret observations of SMBH binaries and to constrain the properties of the surrounding stellar environment.

We address existence of moving gap solitons (traveling localized solutions)in the Gross-Pitaevskii equation with a small periodic potential. Moving gapsolitons are approximated by the explicit localized solutions of thecoupled-mode system. We show however that exponentially decaying travelingsolutions of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation do not generally exist in thepresence of a periodic potential due to bounded oscillatory tails ahead andbehind the moving solitary waves. The oscillatory tails are not accounted inthe coupled-mode formalism and are estimated by using techniques of spatialdynamics and local center-stable manifold reductions. Existence of boundedtraveling solutions of the Gross--Pitaevskii equation with a single bumpsurrounded by oscillatory tails on a finite large interval of the spatial scaleis proven by using these technique. We also show generality of oscillatorytails in other nonlinear equations with a periodic potential.

In this article, we investigate the linearisation properties of finite abelian subgroups within the context of the Cremona group of the plane. The Cremona group, denoting the birational automorphisms of the projective plane, has been extensively studied in algebraic geometry and related fields. Our primary focus lies in understanding the linear behaviour of certain finite abelian subgroups within this group.We begin by exploring the concept of linearisation and its significance in the context of the Cremona group. Linearisation refers to the process of finding a faithful linear representation of a given group, often enabling a deeper analysis of its properties. We aim to establish whether finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona group possess such linearisations.To tackle this question, we employ techniques from algebraic geometry, commutative algebra, and representation theory. We consider the action of abelian subgroups on projective spaces and investigate the existence of linear transformations that faithfully preserve the group structure. The interplay of these linear transformations with the structures of the Cremona group and its subgroups forms a central aspect of our research.Furthermore, we explore the connection between linearisations of finite abelian subgroups and the structure of the Cremona group, seeking to identify any underlying patterns or relationships. We apply rigorous mathematical techniques such as cohomology theory and intersection theory to provide a comprehensive analysis of this intricate relationship.Our results contribute to the understanding of the fundamental properties of finite abelian subgroups within the Cremona group, shedding light on the underlying geometric and algebraic structures at play.

During the last three decades, evidence has mounted that star and planetformation is not an isolated process, but is influenced by current and previousgenerations of stars. Although cool stars form in a range of environments, fromisolated globules to rich embedded clusters, the influences of other stars oncool star and planet formation may be most significant in embedded clusters,where hundreds to thousands of cool stars form in close proximity to OB stars.At the cool stars 14 meeting, a splinter session was convened to discuss therole of environment in the formation of cool stars and planetary systems; withan emphasis on the ''hot'' environment found in rich clusters. We review herethe basic results, ideas and questions presented at the session. We haveorganized this contribution into five basic questions: what is the typicalenvironment of cool star formation, what role do hot star play in cool starformation, what role does environment play in planet formation, what is therole of hot star winds and supernovae, and what was the formation environmentof the Sun? The intention is to review progress made in addressing eachquestion, and to underscore areas of agreement and contention.

The Slon Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) completely changes our understanding of the universe by providing a wide and detailed paradise map. In this study, we use SDSS data to study the variability of celestial objects with different spectral bands across different spectral bands. By analyzing the optical curve of a large number of source samples, we found the rich diversity of variable phenomena in the night sky. Our research focuses on the time and behaviors of stars, galaxies, and stars, thus clarify their inherent characteristics and physical processes. We use the extensive multi -wavelength coverage of SDS to check the color evolution of the variable objects and detect the basic mechanism that promotes its mutation. In addition, we use statistical technology to quantify the universality and properties of different types of degeneration, such as periodicity, upper, transient changes. The study also explores the effects of observation pseudo -image and system uncertainty on detected variable -nature. In addition, we have studied the impact of these discoveries on the investigation of the universe and the large -scale study of the universe. Our results prove that the time dependence of the SDSS tool in capturing the source of celestial bodies is essentially the essential power, and it provides valuable insights for the nature of the variable phenomenon in the night sky. This work lays the foundation for future investigations, and uses SDSS and other surveys to reveal the mystery of the changing universe.

Investigating the decoherence dynamics of complex quantum systems interacting with environments remains a fundamentally important endeavor. This work analyzes a driven multilevel quantum system coupled to a non-Markovian multi-bath reservoir, examining the interplay between dissipation, dephasing, and coherent driving on the reduced system's quasienergy resonances. By systematically varying driving parameters and bath spectral densities, we map out rich decoherence time scale landscapes as a function of bath coupling strengths and bath cut-off frequencies, characterizing intricate MSW resonance signatures and their sensitivity to bath-induced damping rates. Quantitative agreement is found between predictions of our exact non-perturbative numerical simulations and analytical Floquet-Markov master equation approaches in appropriate regimes. Our comprehensive characterization of driven multilevel system decoherence points to new opportunities for harnessing complex bath-engineered reservoir engineering techniques to optimize quantum memory times.

The time-dependent transverse response of stiff polymers, represented asweakly-bending wormlike chains (WLCs), is well-understood on the linear level,where transverse degrees of freedom evolve independently from the longitudinalones. We show that, beyond a characteristic time scale, the nonlinear couplingof transverse and longitudinal motion in an inextensible WLC significantlyweakens the polymer response compared to the widely used linear responsepredictions. The corresponding feedback mechanism is rationalized by scalingarguments and quantified by a multiple scale approach that exploits an inherentseparation of transverse and longitudinal correlation length scales. Crossoverscaling laws and exact analytical and numerical solutions for characteristicresponse quantities are derived for different experimentally relevant setups.Our findings are applicable to cytoskeletal filaments as well as DNA undertension.

Jets causing from active galactic nuclei can distributing vast distances through the intergalactic medium. When these relativistic jets interact with surrounding plasma, they may prepares instabilities. In this analyzing, we surveyed chromohydrodynamical instabilities that can arise at the interface between relativistic astrophysical jets and the ambient gas. Employ analytical theory and numerical simulations, we model the growth of current-driven and kink-type instabilities under conditions predicts in jet environments. Our results demonstrate that these instabilities develop succinctly at early times and aiding to jet deceleration and transverse momentum exchange. However, the jets are able to maintain collimation and penetration over overwhelming scales. Characterizing such instabilities tender insight into jet morphology and influences wide-ranging astrophysical phenomena on galactic to intracluster scales.

Millisecond pulsars (MSPs) are rapidly rotating neutron stars thought to be spun-up by mass accretion from a binary companion. This article presents the discovery and follow-up observations of PSR J1453+1902, an MSP located in an intermediate Galactic latitude. We report the timing characterization of PSR J1453+1902 and find it has a spin period of 2.6 ms, placing it among the most rapidly rotating MSPs known. A comparison of the radio luminosity of PSR J1453+1902 to other known solitary and binary MSP populations shows that solitary pulsars tend to be less radio luminous than their binary counterparts. This finds supports the standard theories of MSP spin-up through mass accretion in a binary system. Studying the properties of solitary MSPs like PSR J1453+1902 provides important tests and constraints on MSP formation and evolution scenarios. Further multi-wavelength observations of this pulsar will help elucidate differences between isolated versus binary MSP populations.

The currently-favored model for long-duration gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) invokesexplosions from the collapse of a massive star down to a black hole: eitherdirectly or through fallback. Those GRBs forming via fallback will produce muchless radioactive nickel, and hence it has been argued (without any realcalculation) that these systems produce dim supernovae. These fallbackblack-hole GRBs have been recently been argued as possible progenitors of anewly discovered set of GRBs lacking any associated supernovae. Here we presentthe first ever radiation-hydrodynamics calculations of the light-curvesproduced in the hypernova explosion by a delayed-fallback gamma-ray burst. Wefind that the bolometric light-curve is dominated by shock-deposited energy,not the decay of radioactive elements. As such, observations of such burstsactually probe the density in the progenitor wind more than it does theproduction of radioactive nickel.

In this study, we investigate the habitat segregation between Lyman break galaxies (LBGs) and Lyman alpha emitters (LAEs) around a quasar at redshift z ~ 5. Using a combination of observational data and simulations, we explore the spatial distribution of these two populations and examine their respective properties. Our results show that LBGs and LAEs exhibit distinct clustering patterns, with LBGs preferentially located in higher density regions and LAEs found in lower density environments. We also find that LBGs have higher star formation rates and larger galaxy sizes compared to LAEs. The observed segregation patterns suggest that LBGs and LAEs may have different formation mechanisms and evolutionary paths. Moreover, the presence of the quasar does not appear to significantly affect the distribution of either population. Our findings provide new insights into the early universe's galaxy formation and evolution, highlighting the complex interplay between gas, dust, and star formation in shaping galaxy properties.

Several stars orbit around a black hole candidate of mass $3.7\times 10^6$M$_{\odot}$, in the region of the Galactic Center (GC). Looking for GeneralRelativistic (GR) periastron shifts is limited by the existence of a stellarcluster around the black hole that would modify the orbits due to classicaleffects that might mask the GR effect. Only if one knows the cluster parameters(its mass and core radius) it is possible to unequivocally deduce the GReffects expected and then test them. In this paper it is shown that theobservation of the proper motion of Sgr A$^ $, $v_{Sgr A^ } = (0.4\pm 0.9)$ kms$^{-1}$ (\citealt{reid2004}), could help us to constrain the clusterparameters significantly and that future measurements of the periastron shiftsfor at least three stars may adequately determine the cluster parameters andthe mass of the black hole.

Impact of Ion Clearing Electrodes on Beam Dynamics in DAFNE Ion clearing electrodes (ICEs) have been employed in DAFNE to mitigate the effects of ion trapping. This paper presents the results of a study on the impact of ICEs on beam dynamics in DAFNE. Measurements of the beam size, emittance, and lifetime were performed to quantify the effect of ICEs. Furthermore, the influence of ICEs on beam stability and Touschek lifetime was investigated. The experimental results are compared with theoretical predictions.

We study ground state properties and excitation spectra for hard-core Bosonson square and triangular lattices, at half filling, using series expansionmethods. Nearest-neighbor repulsion between the Bosons leads to the developmentof short-range density order at the antiferromagnetic wavevector, andsimultaneously a roton minima in the density excitation spectra. On thesquare-lattice, the model maps on to the well studied XXZ model, and the rotongap collapses to zero precisely at the Heisenberg symmetry point, leading tothe well known spectra for the Heisenberg antiferromagnet. On thetriangular-lattice, the collapse of the roton gap signals the onset of thesupersolid phase. Our results suggest that the transition from the superfluidto the supersolid phase maybe weakly first order. We also find several featuresin the density of states, including two-peaks and a sharp discontinuity, whichmaybe observable in experimental realization of such systems.

Ths study investigates the concept of a sudden future singularity of pressure and explored the extent to which it can be reached. Through a comprehensive analysis of existing theories and empirical evidence, we aim to determine the hypothetical distance to this singularity. Utilizing mathematical models and computational simulations, we assess the various factors that may contribute to the formation and intensifisation of pressure singularities. Additionally, we investigate the potential consequences and implications of reaching such a singularity, providing insights into the understanding of extreme physical phenomena and their impact on the surrounding environment.

Existing methods of secure communication such as encryption rely on complex algorithms and large strength requirements for processing. This article proposes novel approaches for interacts and computing that harness ubiquitous thermal noise as an alternative to traditional layout. Thermal noise is visualized to enable totally secure low-power communication through a simple wire without any crypto or external power source needed. A demonstration of zero-power imparted concept and prototypes is described whereby information can be transmitted simply by manipulating the temperature of the shipment wire using natural thermal fluctuations encoded with data. Otherwise, a new computing paradigm is placed where binary operate are performed by a thermal-state processor using just the inherent thermal fluctuations in its elements rather than conventional power-hungry transistors. Collaborator prototypes of the thermal noise communication and computing concepts are presented and analyzed. Their belongings including bandwidth, error-rates, and power consumption are evaluated and confirm the viability of this new thermal-based communications and computing approach. The implications and applications of harnessing ubiquitous thermal fluctuations are widespread, ranging from minimally-powered micro-scale sensors, to exascale computing, and raising profound questions relating physics, information theory and engineering.

This study investigates the photoconductance properties of organic singe-molecule contacts. The field of molecular electronics has gained significant interest Zdue to its potential for developing nanoscale electronic devices. In this work, we fabricated sngle-molecule junctions using an organci molecule as the active element and characterized their conductance under varying illumination conditions. Our experimental results deomnstrate a significant enhancement in the conductance of the organic single-molecule contacts upon photoexcitation. We further analyze the photoconductance behvaior to understand the underlying mechanisms and propose potential applications for light-controlled organic devices. These findings porvide valuable insights into the optoelectronic properties of sigle-molecule junctions, which can pave the way for the design and develpoment of novel photonic devices based on organic materials.

In this article, we surveyed the photos of his $^4 $ 3 -core interaction of the two -plus plus Canada to absorb cross -section. These interactions originated from hand -valid field theory (EFT). $^4 $ HE nucleus is particularly interesting because its complex structure and nuclear have strong correlation.
