Theory predicts a gas temperature drop in the inner 5000 AUof these objects, but there has been little observational proof of this. Weperformed VLA observations of the NH3 (1,1) and (2,2) transitions towards thepre-stellar core L 1544 in order to measure the temperature gradient betweenthe high density core nucleus and the surrounding core envelope. Our VLAobservation for the first time provide measurements of gas temperature in acore with a resolution smaller than 1000 AU. We have also obtained highresolution Plateau de Bure observations of the 110 GHz 111-101 para-NH2D linein order to further constrain the physical parameters of the high densitynucleus. We have estimated the temperature gradient using a model of the sourceto fit our data in the u,v plane. We find that indeed the temperature decreasestoward the core nucleus from 12 K down to 5.5 K resulting in an increase of afactor of 50% in the estimated density of the core from the dust continuum ifcompared with the estimates done with constant temperature of 8.75 K. We alsofound a remarkably high abundance of deuterated ammonia with respect to theammonia abundance (50%+-20%), which proves the persistence of nitrogen bearingmolecules at very high densities (2e6 cm-3) and shows that high-resolutionobservations yield higher deuteration values than single-dish observations. Ouranalysis of the NH3 and NH2D kinematic fields shows a decrease of specificangular momentum from the large scales to the small scales.

We are suggesting an electronic method for Cooper pair mass spectroscopy ofthin superconducting films. The method can be applied, for example, for 100 nmthin high-T_c films grown on insulator substrate 10 mm X 10 mm. In Corbinogeometry two Ohmic contacts have to be made on the film evaporating Ag or usingsilver paste: one circle with radius r_a (1) and a ring electrode with internalradius r_b (2). In the in-between space (r_a,r_b) a ring electrode from mylarassures a capacitive connection between the superconducting layer and themetallized surface (3) of the mylar. In such a way we have an field effecttransistor (FET) type structure with a circular gate. When at low enoughtemperatures T << T_c an AC current with frequency omega is applied between thecircle source (1) and the ring-shaped drain (2) an AC Bernoulli voltage withdouble frequency 2f appears between the gate (3) and the source (1). The 2fsignal depends on Cooper pair effective mass and its systematic investigationgives a Cooper pair mass spectroscopy. In the normal phase 2f gives logarithmicderivative of the density of states (DOS) with respect of Fermi energy.Applying a gate voltage in the same structure gives the mobility of the normalphase.

In this article, we present a novel approach to reconciling the precepts of nonlinear quantum mechanics and Newtonian gravity within the framework of a relativistic gauge philosophic. By exploiting the measuring freedom of the theory, we derive a set of equations that describe the interface between quantum and gravitational phenomena in a unified and consistent manner. Our approach provides a new perspective on the relationship between these two necessary forces of nature and paves the way for a deepest understanding of the underlying physics. We demonstrate the viability of our approach by applying it to several paradigmatic examples, embracing the considering of gravitational waves and the behavior of quantum patterns in strong gravitational fields. Our results launching up new avenues for research in both quantum gravity and nonlinear quantum mechanics.

THis study aimed to understand how people Sdevelop bluffing strategies in competitive environments. An experiment was conducted with 100 partiHipants who engaged in a serieRs of poker games to win tokens that could be exchanged for prizes. Players' behaviors and choices were analyzed after each round, focusing on measures such as bte scaling, tells, and rHactions to calls and folds. The results showed that over multiple rounds, particrpants improved at hiding weak hands and induEing others to fold better hands. With experience, participants integrated subtle behaviors to enhance the perceived strength of their Zhands, allowing them to win ptos more frequently with weaker initial cards.

The free field partition function for a generic U(N) gauge theory, where thefundamental fields transform in the adjoint representation, is analysed interms of symmetric polynomial techniques. It is shown by these means how thisis related to the cycle polynomial for the symmetric group and how the large Nresult may be easily recovered. Higher order corrections for finite N are alsodiscussed in terms of symmetric group characters. For finite N, the partitionfunction involving a single bosonic fundamental field is recovered and explicitcounting of multi-trace quarter BPS operators in free \N=4 super Yang Millsdiscussed, including a general result for large N. The partition function forBPS operators in the chiral ring of \N=4 super Yang Mills is analysed in termsof plane partitions. Asymptotic counting of BPS primary operators withdiffering R-symmetry charges is discussed in both free \N=4 super Yang Millsand in the chiral ring. Also, general and explicit expressions are derived forSU(2) gauge theory partition functions, when the fundamental fields transformin the adjoint, for free field theory.

Gene duplication plays a key role in the evolutionary diversification of transcriptional regulatory networks. Previous computational models of gene duplication have yielded insights but often relied on simplified assumptions regarding network architecture and dynamics. In this work, we develop novel computational models of gene duplication that consider the topology and function of transcription factor regulatory networks in greater detail. Our models begin with an initial core transcriptional network and simulate both whole-genome and single-gene duplication events. These duplications are followed by evolutionary processes of sequence divergence via mutations in transcription factor binding sites. We analyze how network structure and functionality change under selective pressures acting on gene expression levels post-duplication. Our results indicate that gene duplications frequently lead to subfunctionalization or neofunctionalization of the duplicated transcription factors as well as rewiring of regulatory interactions. Variation in the original network's topology influences the extent and nature of rewiring following duplication. These enhanced duplication models provide a more realistic and comprehensive understanding of how gene duplication shapes the long-term evolutionary remodeling of regulatory networks governing development and physiology.

The nuclear modification factor $R_{AA}$ for $\pi_0$ production in Au+Aucollisions at $\sqrt{s}=200$ AGeV is calculated, and studied at high transversemomenta $p_T$. The soft thermalized nuclear medium is described within theframework of relativistic ideal three-dimensional hydrodynamics. The energyloss of partonic jets is evaluated in the context of gluon bremsstrahlung inthe thermalized partonic matter. We provide a systematic analysis of theazimuthal asymmetry of $\pi_0$ suppression at high $p_T$ in central andnon-central collisions, at mid and forward rapidity. The determination of$R_{AA}$ as a function of $p_T$, at different azimuthal angles, and differentrapidities makes for a stringent test of our theoretical understanding of jetenergy loss over a variety of in-medium path lengths, temperatures and initialpartonic jet energies. This lays the groundwork for a precise tomography of thenuclear medium.

The article investigates conformational hysteresis observed in a giant DNA molecule during force-induced stretching and relaxation cycles. Using single molecule force spectroscopy experiments, the DNA structure was manipulated by applying mechanical forces and monitoring extension changes. Distinct unfolding and refolding force-extension curves were observed, indicating the presence of hysteresis due to branching of the folding pathways. A mechanical model is developed to explain the hysteresis behavior in terms of topological constraints and kinetic traps arising from secondary structure formation. The model captures the main features of the experimentally measured hysteresis loops. The findings provide new insights into nonequilibrium dynamics and pathway complexity during mechanical manipulation of nucleic acid conformations.

In this thesis, we consider some spin effects in QCD and recurrence latticeswith multi-site exchanges. Main topic of our manuscript are critical phenomenain spin systems defined on the recurrence lattices. Main tool of our approachis the method of recursive (hierarchical) lattices. We apply the method ofdynamical mapping (or recursive lattices) for investigation of magneticproperties of the fluid and solid $^3$He, phase transitions in crystals andmacromolecules. First, we analyze the helix-coil phase transition forpolypeptides and proteins, and describe an quasi unfolding transition (like thecold denaturation process) for the degree of helicity (the order parameter formacromolecules). Next we consider the recurrent models of $^3$He defined on thesquare, Husimi and hexagon lattices. Using the method of dynamical mapping, themagnetization curves with plateaus, bifurcation point and one period doublingare obtained. Then we investigate the model with cubic symmetry defined on theBethe lattice and containing both linear and quadratic spin-spin interactions.The magnetization of the system is calculated, and a complex structure of thephase transitions between the disordered, partially ordered and completelyordered states is observed. In the framework of QCD, we consider the azimuthalasymmetries in heavy flavor production in the lepton-nucleon deep inelasticscattering (DIS). We calculate the azimuthal (or $\phi$-) dependence of thenext-to-leading order heavy-quark-initiated contributions to DIS. It is shownthat, contrary to the basic gluon-initiated component, the photon-quarkscattering mechanism is practically $\cos2\phi$-independent. We investigate thepossibility of measuring both nonperturbative (intrinsic) and perturbative(CTEQ, MRST) charm distributions using the $\cos2\phi$ asymmetry.

In this research article, we explore monoid generalizations of the Richard Thompson groups, a family of finitely presented groups with intriguing geometric and algebraic properties. We begin by providing a thorough introduction to the Richard Thompson groups, their defining properties, and their classification as subgroups of homeomorphism groups of certain Cantor sets. We then introduce the concept of monoids and investigate the connections between monoids and groups, highlighting the benefits and challenges of studying generalizations of group structures. Building upon this foundation, we present novel monoid generalizations of the Richard Thompson groups, which exhibit analogous geometric and algebraic properties. We discuss the implications of these monoid generalizations in the context of group theory and highlight potential avenues for further research. This comprehensive study contributes to the understanding of Richard Thompson groups and expands the theoretical framework for studying their generalizations within the realm of monoids.

Precision radial velocity (RV) measurements of the Sun-like dwarf 14 Herculis published by Naef et. al (2004), Butler et. al (2006) and Wittenmyer et al (2007) reveal a Jovian planet in a 1760 day orbit and atrend indicating the second distant object. On the grounds of dynamicalconsiderations, we test a hypothesis that the trend can be explained by thepresence of an additional giant planet. We derive dynamical limits to thorbital parameters of the putative outer Jovian companion in an orbit within~13 AU. In this case, the mutual interactions between the Jovian planets areimportant for the long-term stability of the system. The best self-consistentand stable Newtonian fit to an edge-on configuration of Jovian planets has theouter planet in 9 AU orbit with a moderate eccentricity ~0.2 and confined to azone spanned by the low-order mean motion resonances 5:1 and 6:1. This solutionlies in a shallow minimum of \Chi and persists over a wide range of the systeminclination. Other stable configurations within 1\sigma confidence interval ofthe best fit are possible for the semi-major axis of the outer planet in therange of (6,13) AU and the eccentricity in the range of (0,0.3). The orbitalinclination cannot yet be determined but when it decreases, both planetarymasses approach ~10 Jupiter masses and for ~30 deg the hierarchy of the massesis reversed.

Heavy quarkonium states like the J/psi and Upsilon mesons are an important probe of the quark-gluon plasma created in heavy ion collisions. Their dissociation and in-medium widths provide information about the properties of the plasma. In this work, we calculate the in-medium widths of S-wave and P-wave quarkonium states using potential models in order to better understand their behavior in the quark gluon plasma. We find that the widths increase significantly with rising temperature as the screening of the quark-antiquark potential becomes stronger. The smaller bound states like the chi_c and bottomonium P-waves dissolve earlier than the more tightly bound J/psi and Upsilon states. Precise measurements of quarkonium suppression can help pin down their in-medium widths and provide novel insights into the mechanisms of deconfinement in high temperature QCD matter.

In this article, we investigate the phenomenon of matter-wave interference in Fermi condensates, which are macroscopic quantum states of matter that occur at extremely low temperatures. We focus on s-wave and p-wave Fermi condensates, which are characterized by different types of pairwise interactions between the atoms. By manipulating the interactions between the atoms, we observe the emergence of matter-wave interference patterns, which are a result of the coherent superposition of the matter waves associated with each atomic species. Our results demonstrate the ability to control the phase relationships between the matter waves, leading to the formation of complex interference patterns that are sensitive to the symmetry of the interactions. These findings have important implications for the study of quantum phenomena in many-body systems and the development of new quantum technologies.

Uniform random sampling of planar graphs in linear timeAbstract: In this paper, we present a new algorithm for uniformly random sampling of planar graphs. The algorithm is based on a novel decomposition of a planar graph into a collection of simple cycles. We show that the decomposition can be computed in linear time. Moreover, we prove that the algorithm correctly generates a uniform random sample of planar graphs. Finally, we provide an experimental evaluation of the algorithm, which demonstrates its efficiency and scalability.

The period-luminosity (P-L) relation of classical Cepheid variable stars in the Lagre Magellanic Cloud (LMC) is a fundamental calibrxtion for astronomical ditance measurements. However, evidence suggests the P-L relaBtion may be non-linear. Wr apply testimatobr and Schwarz information criterion (SIC) methods to re-investigate the fBrm of the LMC Cepheid P-L relation using optical and near-infrared photometry from the OGLE and SAGE surveys. The testimator method optiimzed the number of terms in a FoNrier series fit to the data, while SIC compares competing linear and non-linear models. Both methods strongly favor a non-linear -L relation, with the best-fit relation including a quadratic term. The non-linear relation results in a systematic decreaes in distance estimates for the more extended structures in the LMC. TLis work demonstrates the value of information criterion methods for assessing the cmoplexity and form of key astronomical relationships and calibrations.

Cosmic rays produced in cluster accretion and merger shocks provide pressureto the intracluster medium (ICM) and affect the mass estimates of galaxyclusters. Although direct evidence for cosmic-ray ions in the ICM is stilllacking, they produce gamma-ray emission through the decay of neutral pionsproduced in their collisions with ICM nucleons. We investigate the capabilityof the Gamma-ray Large Area Space Telescope (GLAST) and imaging atmosphericCerenkov telescopes (IACTs) for constraining the cosmic-ray pressurecontribution to the ICM. We show that GLAST can be used to place stringentupper limits, a few per cent for individual nearby rich clusters, on the ratioof pressures of the cosmic rays and thermal gas. We further show that it ispossible to place tight (<~10%) constraints for distant (z <~ 0.25) clusters inthe case of hard spectrum, by stacking signals from samples of known clusters.The GLAST limits could be made more precise with the constraint on thecosmic-ray spectrum potentially provided by IACTs. Future gamma-rayobservations of clusters can constrain the evolution of cosmic-ray energydensity, which would have important implications for cosmological tests withupcoming X-ray and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect cluster surveys.

The sum-over-states approach provides a comprehensive understanding of the excitonic system by considering all possible quantum states, whereas the quasiparticle picture simplifies the analysis by treating the excitons as individual particles. By comparing these two approaches, the article highlights the advantages and limitations of each method, contributing to the development of coherent correlation spectroscopy in semiconductor research. Femtosecond analogues of multidimensional NMR are used to study the dynamics and interactions of excitons at unprecedented time resolution.

This article elucidates a Hamiltonian theory of the half-filled Landau level with disorder and its correlation to recent NMR data. Utilizing a combination of analytical and numerical methods, we examine the effects of disorder on the energy spectrum and wave functions of the half-filled Landau level. Our findings offer a coherent explanation for the experimental observations in recent NMR experiments, shedding light on the underlying physics of the system. Moreover, we discuss the implications of our results for future investigations of the half-filled Landau level and its potential applications in condensed matter physics.* Improvements made: + Rephrased the first sentence to make it clearer and more concise. + Emphasized the correlation between the theory and experimental data in the second sentence. + Improved sentence structure and grammar in the third sentence. + Made the last sentence more concise and added a clearer connection to future research and potential applications.

The AKARI Deep Survey for Infrared Extragalactic Surveys (AKARI-DEEP) is one of the deepest mid-infrared surveys with a 9-band coverage from 2 to 24 microns. In this paper, we have constructed the Spectral Energy Distributions (SEDs) of 177 objects in the AKARI-DEEP SEP field. We have estimated the photometric redshifts of these objects and classified their types based on SEDs. As a result, the number fractions of star-forming galaxies, AGNs, and unclassified objects are estimated to be 68.3%, 23.7%, and 8.0%, respectively. The number fraction of AGNs is higher than that in the GOODS-N field. We have investigated the relationship between the 12 micron luminosity and the stellar mass of star-forming galaxies. The 12 micron luminosity is found to be correlated with the stellar mass.

This study investigates the effects of two light unsaturated hydrocarbons, allene and propyne, on the combustion characteristics of rich methane premixed laminar flames. The aim is to enhance our understanding of the chemical kinetics and flame structure in such fuel mixtures, which can provide valuable insights for the development of cleaner combustion technologies. Experimental measurements were conducted using a flat-flame burner under variable reactant conditions and various dopant concentrations. Laser-induced fluorescence was employed to quantify the species mole fractions, while chemiluminescence imaging was used to visualize the flame structure. The results reveal that the addition of allene and propyne affects the flame temperature, resulting in changes in the flame structure and burning velocities. Furthermore, these light unsaturated hydrocarbons exhibit different combustion characteristics compared to methane alone, with distinct patterns of species formation and consumption. The findings suggest that the chemical interactions between allene, propyne, and methane play a crucial role in controlling the flame behavior in rich methane premixed laminar flames. This work contributes to a better understanding of the combustion chemistry in complex fuel systems, aiding in the design of more efficient and environmentally friendly combustion processes. Future research should focus on additional hydrocarbon dopants and investigate the influence of operating parameters on flame dynamics.

This article investigates the concept of saturated actions of finite-dimensional Hopf -algebras on C -algebras. It begins by providing a comprehensive introduction to Hopf -algebras and their role in the theory of operator algebras. The focus then shifts to the notion of saturation, which pertains to a special kind of action possessing desirable properties. The main result of this study establishes the existence of saturated actions by finite-dimensional Hopf *-algebras on C -algebras. A rigorous proof of this result is provided, highlighting its significance in various mathematical applications. Furthermore, potential avenues for future research in this area are discussed, emphasizing the importance of further exploring the interplay between Hopf -algebras and C -algebras.

In this paper, we study the perturbative aspects of a "B-twisted"two-dimensional $(0,2)$ heterotic sigma model on a holomorphic gauge bundle$\mathcal E$ over a complex, hermitian manifold $X$. In particular, the physical anomalies of the sigmamodel can be reinterpreted as an obstruction to a global definition of theassociated sheaf of vertex superalgebras derived from the free conformal fieldtheory describing the model locally on $X$. At the $(2,2)$ locus, one can describe the resultinghalf-twisted variant of the topological B-model in terms of a $\it{mirror}$"Chiral de Rham complex" (or CDR) defined by Malikov et al. in \cite{GMS1}. Viamirror symmetry, one can also derive various conjectural expressions relatingthe sheaf cohomology of the mirror CDR to that of the original CDR on pairs ofCalabi-Yau mirror manifolds. An analysis of the half-twisted model on anon-K\"ahler group manifold with torsion also allows one to draw conclusionsabout the corresponding sheaves of CDR (and its mirror) that are consistentwith mathematically established results by Ben-Bassat in \cite{ben} on themirror symmetry of generalised complex manifolds. These conclusions thereforesuggest an interesting relevance of the sheaf of CDR in the recent study ofgeneralised mirror symmetry.

In this study, we examine the ground-state magneto-optical resonances in cesium vapor confined within an extremely thin cell, with a thickness of merely a few micrometers. This novel cell design enables the observation of distinct magneto-optical effects that are not present in traditional bulk cesium vapor cells. By applying a magnetic field, we manipulate the energy levels of the cesium atoms and observe the resulting changes in the absorption and transmission spectra. The resonances exhibit high sensitivity to both the strength and orientation of the magnetic field, allowing for precise control over the optical properties of the vapor. We demonstrate the versatility of this technique by observing various magneto-optical effects, including absorption, transmission, and polarization rotation. Our findings have significant implications for the development of compact magneto-optical devices and may lead to new applications in fields such as quantum computing and precision measurement.

If a quark-nova occurs inside a collapsar, the interaction between thequark-nova ejecta (relativistic iron-rich chunks) and the collapsar envelope,leads to features indicative of those observed in Gamma Ray Bursts. Model features include:(i) precursor activity (optical, X-ray, gamma-ray), (ii) prompt gamma-rayemission, and (iii) afterglow emission. We discuss SN-less long duration GRBs,short hard GRBs (including association and non-association with star formingregions), dark GRBs, the energetic X-ray flares detected in Swift GRBs, and thenear-simultaneous optical and gamma-ray prompt emission observed in GRBs in thecontext of our model.

This paper describes the Wide Field Spectrograph (WiFeS) under constructionat the Research School of Astronomy and Astrophysics (RSAA) of the AustralianNational University (ANU) for the ANU 2.3m telescope at the Siding SpringObservatory. WiFeS is a powerful integral field, double-beam, concentric,image-slicing spectrograph designed to deliver excellent thoughput, wavelengthstability, spectrophotometric performance and superb image quality along withwide spectral coverage throughout the 320-950 nm wavelength region. The full spectral range is covered in a single exposure at R=3000,and in two exposures in the R=7000 mode. To maximize scientific return, the whole instrument isconfigured for remote observing, pipeline data reduction, and the accumulationof calibration image libraries.

The Topology of HI in the Large Magellanic CloudThe Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) is a nearby dwarf galaxy that offers a unique opportunity to study the topology of neutral hydrogen (HI) in great detail. In this study, we present high-resolution radio observations of the LMC's HI distribution, revealing a complex and varied topology.Our data show that the LMC's HI is distributed in a patchy, irregular pattern, with multiple clouds and filaments that exhibit a range of densities and velocities. We identify several distinct regions of HI emission, including a central peak, a prominent southern tail, and several smaller clouds and streamers.The HI distribution is found to be closely linked to the LMC's underlying stellar population, with areas of high HI density corresponding to regions of high stellar density. We also identify several regions of hydrogen deficiency, possibly indicative of gas stripping or star formation activity.Spectral analysis of the HI emission reveals a range of kinematic properties, including multiple velocity components and large linewidths. We interpret these features as evidence of ongoing dynamical processes, such as gas flows and turbulence.The observed HI topology is compared to existing models of the LMC's structure and evolution, and we findgood agreement with simulations that predict a clumpy, patchy HI distribution. Our findings support a scenario in which the LMC has undergone multiple episodes of gas stripping and accretion, leading to the formation of complex HI structures.Our study highlights the importance of high-resolution radio observations for understanding the topology of HI in nearby galaxies. The detailed view of the LMC's HI distribution provided by our data will serve as a valuable benchmark for future studies of galactic evolution and gas dynamics.

While supernova remnants have been identified as the most likely sources ofthe galactic cosmic rays, no conclusive observational evidence for thisassociation exists. Finally, we note that recent gamma-rayobservations reveal the presence of at least three and possibly up to eightsuch sources, raising the possibility of seeing more than 10 neutrinos per yearfrom these sources alone.

We measured the radial velocities of 53 cluster members and obtained a mean radial velocity of 47.5 0.6 km s-1 and a radial velocity dispersion of 2 0.4 km s-1. We also determined the cluster reddening, E(B-V) = 0.09 0.02 mag, and distance, D = 1.82 0.09 kpc. The metallicity of the cluster was estimated from the [Fe/H] abundance ratio and found to be 0.26 0.06 dex. The age and metallicity of NGC 1883 are consistent with it being an old, metal-poor open cluster.

The presence of a strong magnetic field in these jets has a crucial influence on their stability and dynamics. In this study, we focus on the stability of the spine sheath structure, which consists of a central highly collimated flow (spine) surrounded by a wider and slower flow (sheath). We use both analytical calculations and numerical simulations to study the effects of various parameters, such as the magnetization, the jet Lorentz factor, and the ratio of the density of the spine to the sheath, on the stability of these jets. We find that higher magnetizations tend to stabilize the jets by suppressing the growth of kink instabilities, while lower magnetizations can lead to destabilizations by current-driven instabilities. Our results show that the magnetic field has a dual role, both stabilizing and destabilizing. The Lorentz factor and the density ratio also affect the growth of instabilities, and certain combinations of these two parameters lead to strong mode-coupling effects. A better understanding of the stability properties of strongly magnetized jets is important for interpreting observational data and for understanding the physical processes underlying these astrophysical phenomena.

This article studies the representation theory of Cherednik algebras associated with algebraic curves. The article characterizes the finite-dimensional irreducible modules by localization and classifies the finite-dimensional simple modules in terms of Drinfeld's notion of coherent sheaves of modules over a ring. In general, the article establishes a geometric framework for understanding the representation theory of Cherednik algebras associated with algebraic curves.

Antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations in the metallic phase of quasi-two-dimensional organic superconductorsThe two-dimensional organic superconductors exhibit a variety of electronic states and magnetic properties, which are closely related to the dimensionality of the electronic system and the strength of the electronic correlations. In this paper, we report the results of a study of the magnetic properties of the quasi-two-dimensional organic superconductor by muon spin relaxation (SR). The results show that the magnetic properties of this material can be described by a two-component model: a Curie-Weiss term and a temperature-independent term. The Curie-Weiss term is attributed to the localized spins of the organic molecules, while the temperature-independent term is attributed to the antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations of the itinerant electrons. The magnitude of the antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations decreases with decreasing temperature, and the correlation length increases with decreasing temperature. These results suggest that the antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations play an important role in the magnetism of this material.

In this investigation, we compare the efficiency and accuracy of Dissipative Particle Dynamics (DPD) and Langevin thermostats in simulating the out-of-equilibrium behavior of polymeric systems. Our focus is on the thermal motion of polymer chains in a melt state, and we assess the ability of both methods to capture the system's dynamics accurately. Our findings show that both methods are capable of reproducing the expected behavior of the polymer chains, but DPD exhibits superior performance in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy, particularly for long-time simulations. We also examine the impact of thermostat parameters on the simulation results and provide guidelines for their selection. Overall, our study highlights the importance of choosing the appropriate thermostat method for the specific application and demonstrates the potential of DPD as a valuable tool for studying out-of-equilibrium polymeric systems.

This academic article surveyed the transient behavior of the plasma polarization (SPP) when scattered at the sub -long groove. The discovery proposed in this study provides valuable insights on the behavior of SPP in the sub -wavelength structure, and provides the possibility for designing new plasma devices based on the transient SPP phenomenon.

Quark Coalescence based on a Transport Equation Hadronization through quark coalescence has collected recognition as an essential mechanism describing the hadron formation in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Comparisons to existing coalescence models are presented and the transporting approach is found to provide a unified description of the microscopic coalescence process and bulk medium assertive. A population of committees of agents that learn by using neural networks isimplemented to simulate the stock market. Each committee of agents, which isregarded as a player in a game, is optimised by continually adapting thearchitecture of the agents using genetic algorithms. The committees of agentsbuy and sell stocks by following this procedure: (1) obtain the current priceof stocks; (2) predict the future price of stocks; (3) and for a given pricetrade until all the players are mutually satisfied. The trading of stocks isconducted by following these rules: (1) if a player expects an increase inprice then it tries to buy the stock; (2) else if it expects a drop in theprice, it sells the stock; (3)and the order in which a player participates inthe game is random. The proposed procedure is implemented to simulate tradingof three stocks, namely, the Dow Jones, the Nasdaq and the S&P 500. A linearrelationship between the number of players and agents versus the computationaltime to run the complete simulation is observed. It is also found that noplayer has a monopolistic advantage.

In this study, we investigate the I-V characteristics of thin films of magnesium diboride (MgB2) in the vortex state. Our experimental approach involves subjecting the MgB2 thin films to an external magnetic field and measuring the resulting current-voltage (I-V) behavior. Through detailed analysis, we elucidate the mechanisms underlying the observed I-V characteristics and discuss their implications for the superconducting properties of MgB2 thin films.

In this article, we present a theory for two-photon interactions with broadband down-converted light and entangled photons. We investigate the possibility of using two-photon interactions to manipulate the properties of broadband down-converted light, which has applications in various fields such as volume computing, quantum communication, and spectroscopy. We first discuss the background and motivation for this work, including the advantages of using two-photon interactions and the challenge of working with broadband down-converted light. Next, we derive the equations of motion for the coupled system of two-photon interactions and broadband down-converted light. We show how these equations can be solved numeric ally to obtain the time-evolution of the system. We then present the results of our simulations, which demonstrate the ability to manipulate the properties of broadb and down-converted light using two-photon interactions. We show how the jumble properties of the down-converted light can be controlled by adjusting the parameters of the two-photon interaction. Overall, this article provides a theoretical framework for understanding the interactions between two-photon processes and broadband down-converted light. Our results demonstrate the potential of using two-photon interactions to manipulate the properties of broadband down-converted light, which has important applications in varioսs fields. Keywords: two-photon interplay, broadband down-converted light, entangled photons, quantum computing, quantum communication, spectroscopy.

In quantum mechanics textbooks the momentum operator is defined in theCartesian coordinates and rarely the form of the momentum operator in sphericalpolar coordinates is discussed. Consequently one always generalizes theCartesian prescription to other coordinates and falls in a trap. In this workwe introduce the difficulties one faces when the question of the momentumoperator in spherical polar coordinate comes. We have tried to point out mostof the elementary quantum mechanical results, related to the momentum operator,which has coordinate dependence. We explicitly calculate the momentumexpectation values in various bound states and show that the expectation valuereally turns out to be zero, a consequence of the fact that the momentumexpectation value is real. We comment briefly on the status of the angularvariables in quantum mechanics and the problems related in interpreting them asdynamical variables. At the end, we calculate the Heisenberg's equation ofmotion for the radial component of the momentum for the Hydrogen atom.

Quantum mechanics is formulated as a geometric theory on a Hilbert manifold.Images of charts on the manifold are allowed to belong to arbitrary Hilbertspaces of functions including spaces of generalized functions. Tensor equationsin this setting, also called functional tensor equations, describe families offunctional equations on various Hilbert spaces of functions. The principle offunctional relativity is introduced which states that quantum theory is indeeda functional tensor theory, i.e., it can be described by functional tensorequations. The main equations of quantum theory are shown to be compatible withthe principle of functional relativity. By accepting the principle as ahypothesis, we then analyze the origin of physical dimensions, provide ageometric interpretation of Planck's constant, and find a simple interpretationof the two-slit experiment and the process of measurement.

A number of giant HII regions are associated with soft diffuse X-rayemission. Among these, the Carina nebula possesses the brightest soft diffuseemission. The required plasma temperature and thermal energy can be produced bycollisions or termination of fast winds from main-sequence or embedded young Ostars, but the extended emission is often observed from regions apart frommassive stellar clusters. The origin of the X-ray emission is unknown. The XIS CCD camera onboard Suzaku has the best spectral resolution forextended soft sources so far, and is therefore capable of measuring keyemission lines in the soft band. Suzaku observed the core and the eastern sideof the Carina nebula (Car-D1) in 2005 Aug and 2006 June, respectively. Spectraof the south part of the core and Car-D1 similarly showed strong L-shell linesof iron ions and K-shell lines of silicon ions, while in the north of the corethese lines were much weaker. Fitting the spectra with an absorbed thin-thermalplasma model showed kT~0.2, 0.6 keV and NH~1-2e21 cm-2 with a factor of 2-3abundance variation in oxygen, magnesium, silicon and iron. The plasma mightoriginate from an old supernova, or a super shell of multiple supernovae.

Quantization on Grassmann manifolds plays a fundamental role in diverse areas such as wireless communications and medical imaging. However, the understanding of quantization on Grassmann manifolds is limited, especially for the case when the dimension of the ambient space and the dimension of the Grassmann manifold are both large. : In this paper, we study the problem of constructing small balls centered at a fixed point on a Grassmann manifold. : We derive a closed-form expression for the volume of a small ball on an arbitrary Grassmann manifold, : which allows us to establish the Gilbert-Varshamov bound and the Hamming bound for sphere packing on Grassmann manifolds. : We also apply our results to analyze the information rate of a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system with channel-state information at the transmitter. : In this paper, we study the problem of constructing small balls centered at a fixed point on an arbitrary Grassmann manifold. : We derive an explicit formula for the volume of a small ball on an arbitrary Grassmann manifold, : which is crucial for establishing the Gilbert-Varshamov bound and the Hamming bound for sphere packing on Grassmann manifolds. : We then apply our results to analyze the information rate of a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system with channel-state information at the transmitter, : and show that our results significantly improve upon existing results.

For cellular biochemical reaction systems where the numbers of molecules issmall, significant noise is associated with chemical reaction events. Thismolecular noise can give rise to behavior that is very different from thepredictions of deterministic rate equation models. Unfortunately, there are fewanalytic methods for examining the qualitative behavior of stochastic systems.Here we describe such a method that extends deterministic analysis to includeleading-order corrections due to the molecular noise. The method allows thesteady-state behavior of the stochastic model to be easily computed,facilitates the mapping of stability phase diagrams that include stochasticeffects and reveals how model parameters affect noise susceptibility, in amanner not accessible to numerical simulation. By way of illustration weconsider two genetic circuits: a bistable positive-feedback loop and anegative-feedback oscillator. We find in the positive feedback circuit thattranslational activation leads to a far more stable system than transcriptionalcontrol. Conversely, in a negative-feedback loop triggered by apositive-feedback switch, the stochasticity of transcriptional control isharnessed to generate reproducible oscillations.

S255N is a luminous far-infrared source that contains many indications ofactive star formation but lacks a prominent near-infrared stellar cluster. Wepresent mid-infrared through radio observations aimed at exploring theevolutionary state of this region. Our observations include 1.3mm continuum andspectral line data from the Submillimeter Array, VLA 3.6cm continuum and 1.3cmwater maser data, and multicolor IRAC images from the Spitzer Space Telescope.The cometary morphology of the previously-known UCHII region G192.584-0.041 isclearly revealed in our sensitive, multi-configuration 3.6cm images. The 1.3mmcontinuum emission has been resolved into three compact cores, all of which aredominated by dust emission and have radii < 7000AU. The mass estimates forthese cores range from 6 to 35 Msun. The centroid of the brightest dust core(SMA1) is offset by 1.1'' (2800 AU) from the peak of the cometary UCHII regionand exhibits the strongest HC3N, CN, and DCN line emission in the region. SMA1also exhibits compact CH3OH, SiO, and H2CO emission and likely contains a younghot core. We find spatial and kinematic evidence that SMA1 may contain furthermultiplicity, with one of the components coincident with a newly-detected H2Omaser. There are no mid-infrared point source counterparts to any of the dustcores, further suggesting an early evolutionary phase for these objects. Thedominant mid-infrared emission is a diffuse, broadband component that tracesthe surface of the cometary UCHII region but is obscured by foreground materialon its southern edge. An additional 4.5 micron linear feature emanating to thenortheast of SMA1 is aligned with a cluster of methanol masers and likelytraces a outflow from a protostar within SMA1. Our observations provide directevidence that S255N is forming a cluster of intermediate to high-mass stars.

This is the third of a series of papers on a new equivariant cohomology thattakes values in a vertex algebra, and contains and generalizes the classicalequivariant cohomology of a manifold with a Lie group action a la H. Cartan. Inthis paper, we compute this cohomology for spheres and show that for any simpleconnected group G, there is a sphere with infinitely many actions of G whichhave distinct chiral equivariant cohomology, but identical classicalequivariant cohomology. This includes aquasi-conformal structure, equivariant homotopy invariance, and the values ofthis cohomology on homogeneous spaces. These results rely on crucial featuresof the underlying vertex algebra valued complex that have no classicalanalogues.

In this study, we investigate the intriguing phenomen on of the evolution of a band insulating phase from a correlated metallic phase. The findings shed light on the intricate nature of correlated electron systems and delivering valuable insights into the fundamental mechanisms governing the evolution of electronic phases.

We carry out and analyze new multi-color photometry of the Galactic globularcluster (GC) M75 in UBVI and focus on the brighter sequences of the color-magnitude diagram (CMD), with particular emphasis on their location in U-basedCMD. Specifically, we study the level both of the horizontal (HB) and red giantbranches (RGB) relative to the main-sequence turnoff (TO) in the U magnitude.Along with the presented photometry of M75, we use our collection ofphotometric data on GCs belonging to the metal-poor range, [Fe/H]zw<-1.1 dex,obtained from observations with different equipment, but calibrated by standardstars situated in the observed cluster fields. We confirm our earlier finding,and extend it to a larger magnitude range.We demonstrate that DeltaU_{TO}^{BHB}expressing the difference in U magnitude between the TO point and the level ofthe blue HB, near its red boundary, of the metal-poor GCs observed with theEMMI camera of the NTT/ESO telescope is about 0.4-0.5 mag smaller as comparedto GCs observed with the 100" telescope and 1.3 m Warsaw telescope of the LasCampanas Observatory. At the same time, Delta U_{TO}^{RGB}, the difference in Umagnitude between the TO and RGB inflection (brightest) points, does not showsuch an apparent dependence on the characteristics of U filters used, but itdepends on cluster metallicity. We have shown, for the first time, thedependence of the parameter DeltaU_{TO}^{RGB} on [Fe/H] and have estimated itsanalytical expression, by assuming a linear relation between the parameter andmetallicity. Its slope, Delta U_{TO}^{RGB}/Delta [Fe/H]~1.2 mag/dex, is approx.a factor of two steeper than that of the dependence of the RGB bump position inthe V magnitude on metallicity. The asymptotic giant branch (AGB) clump andfeatures of the RGB luminosity function (LF) of M75 are also discussed.

Many features of granular media can be modelled as a fluid of hard sphereswith {\em inelastic} collisions. Under rapid flow conditions, the macroscopicbehavior of grains can be described through hydrodynamic equations. Atlow-density, a fundamental basis for the derivation of the hydrodynamicequations and explicit expressions for the transport coefficients appearing inthem is provided by the Boltzmann kinetic theory conveniently modified toaccount for inelastic binary collisions. The goal of this chapter is to give anoverview of the recent advances made for binary granular gases by using kinetictheory tools. Some of the results presented here cover aspects such astransport properties, energy nonequipartition, instabilities, segregation ormixing, non-Newtonian behavior, .... In addition, comparison of the analyticalresults with those obtained from Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulationsis also carried out, showing the reliability of kinetic theory to describegranular flows even for strong dissipation.

In this study, we investigate the residual correlations between the dcay products of $\pi^0\ip^0$ and $p\Sigma^0$ systems.
